- **V1-056 sub-slice 8e-2, the Final Settlement's Credit applications (BR-CREDIT-006, BR-CREDIT-008, BR-SETTLE-004, BR-SETTLE-009, BR-SETTLE-012, BR-SETTLE-013, BR-AUTH-010, DL-032; owner answers 1 to 3 to Q-2026-10-06-32 and to Q-2026-10-05-29; migration `20261028_93`):** `app.post_final_settlement_credit_application(property, approver, settlement, draft, step)` is a new internal writer (no grant to any role, like the 8d Refund writer); the Settlement confirm (8e-3) calls it once for each Customer Credit step of the confirmed `FINAL_SETTLEMENT` draft, in the draft's order, after its decision and before any Deposit application or Refund. It writes the same header and detail rows as `app.post_credit_application`: on an Invoice with Rent or Service lines the Rent-first proposal with its trace (the existing Credit check re-runs the proposal) or the Customer's designation recorded as text (BR-CREDIT-006, owner answer 1 to Q-2026-10-05-29), a direct Late-payment Charge, and on an Invoice without Rent or Service lines the existing `OTHER_APPLICABLE_OBLIGATION` basis with `OTHER_CONFIRMED` details, which no writer produced before. Every existing Credit trigger runs unchanged on these rows, so a Customer's Credit pays only that Customer's obligations (BR-CREDIT-008; owner answer to Q-2026-10-05-29), within its available value, the target balance and the chronology. The row records the Settlement link in `customer_credit_applications.final_settlement_id` (docs/004 DB-CREDIT-002; the NULL-only CHECK becomes a foreign key, a relaxing change) and the Settlement's `financial.approve` confirmation as its authorization (the authorization CHECK accepts `financial.approve` only on a row with a Settlement, `credits.apply` on every other row). A source check before insert and a deferred check at commit (as the 8d Refunds) tie the row to its step: an open Settlement of a terminated Lease, a time not before the Settlement started (as the 8a and 8d rows; review round 2), a human approver with an active account (the application checks `financial.approve`), a target of the Settlement Lease, the step of a draft that waits or is confirmed by the same approver, matched exactly (Credit, target, amount, designation and the basis BR-CREDIT-006 gives), committed only with that draft CONFIRMED under `financial.approve` by the same approver and exactly one detail on the step's obligation. Owner answer 3: a reversal of a Credit application the Settlement made is refused (SQLSTATE `P5S01`, mapped to a conflict by the Credit service) before every other reversal check, so neither the one-call reversal nor the credit Adjustment excess path can reverse it; ordinary Credit applications and their reversals stay open after closure (owner answer 7 to Q-2026-10-05-20). Choices within the plan: (1) the writer takes the draft and the step's position and reads the step itself; the application's `id` is derived from the draft and the step (`app.final_settlement_credit_application_id`, an md5-based uuid), so each step is written at most once and the checks find the step from the row, and the detail's `calculation_trace` names the draft and the step; no new column or table, so the Credit application resource and its JSON keep their shape; (2) Customer Credit comes first (DL-032 step 2, BR-SETTLE-004): no Settlement Credit application once the Settlement has a Deposit application or a Refund (it refuses only rows no writer could create before); (3) the writer takes the locks of `app.post_credit_application` in its order after the Settlement row, and its instant is strictly later than every earlier event of the Credit and the target, so Credit steps that follow each other in one transaction keep the existing chronology checks; (4) like `app.post_credit_application` it defers the header's checks until its detail is written, but it names only its own four deferred checks (as the 8d Refund writer does; review round 1) and never sets anything IMMEDIATE again, so the other constraints of the confirm transaction keep their mode (sub-slice 8d); (5) the reversal refusal reuses `P5S01`, the closed-Settlement refusal of 8e-1, because a Settlement Credit application exists only with a Settlement the confirm closes in the same transaction; the Invoice service already maps it to a conflict (credit Adjustment excess path). No closed Settlement and no Settlement Credit application exist before 8e-3, so nothing changes for existing data. No HTTP route (slice 11e); `POST /credit-applications/{id}/reverse` answers 409 for such an application (docs/005 API-063). For the owner's information (review round 1): while a Settlement Credit application stands, its Customer Credit and its source Payment cannot be reversed either (existing rules: their applications must be reversed first), so a Payment that bounces after its Credit paid Settlement debt waits for the post-settlement corrections (slice 10), as a Payment whose Deposit a Deposit application used already does.

- **V1-056 sub-slice 8e-3, Final Settlement confirm and close (BR-SETTLE-004, BR-SETTLE-007, BR-SETTLE-008, BR-SETTLE-009, BR-SETTLE-011, BR-SETTLE-012, BR-SETTLE-015, BR-SETTLE-016, BR-SETTLE-017, BR-AUTH-010, BR-DEP-023, BR-DEP-026, BR-DEP-027, BR-CREDIT-006, BR-CREDIT-008, DL-032; DB-SETTLE-001, 002, 004, 006; owner answers to Q-2026-10-05-20, -23, -24, Q-2026-10-06-32 (answer 4), -33 (answers 2 and 3) and -34; migration `20261029_94`):** `app.confirm_final_settlement_draft` (financial role; `FinalSettlementService.confirm` checks `financial.approve`) confirms a pending `FINAL_SETTLEMENT` draft and closes its Settlement in one transaction, as docs/004 DB-SETTLE-001 describes: the locks of the plan notes, the digest and plan check again under them (a stale draft is refused with `P5S02` and stays pending), the decision, the Customer Credit steps, the Deposit applications, the Refunds in Deposit id order, the closure checks, the snapshots, the single closure and one `final_settlement.closed` audit event naming the draft and every record written. A Settlement is never reopened; the closing balance stays on the ledger of the Customer named on each obligation; nothing is written off. Choices within the plan: (1) lock position of the Lease row (8e-2 round-3 note): first among the row locks, after the Settlement draft lock, because the Lease-first writers (the start of a Settlement, termination and move-out commands, the unpaid-Initial and hand-back resolutions) then wait instead of deadlocking, and a new charge whose guard ran before the Settlement started waits through its key lock on the Lease; the Settlement confirm reports it as a conflict; (2) the stale refusal has its own SQLSTATE `P5S02`, and the service reports it, and a writer's 23514, 23505 or Credit proposal code (P5101, P5102, P5104), as `FinalSettlementStaleDraftError`, a conflict; an inactive approver is refused first by `app.require_invoice_command_actor` (P4506), an authorization error; (3) the Deposit application and Refund ids are derived from the draft and the step or Deposit (md5-based, as the 8e-2 Credit application id), so the decision records every id before the writers run and an exact repeat replays; (4) a Deposit application records the draft reason, and a remaining Pet Deposit application (step 5) the staff reason of its decision; a Refund records the draft reason; (5) every writer's deferred checks fire (`SET CONSTRAINTS ALL IMMEDIATE`) after the last writer and before the closure, the snapshot checks are set back to DEFERRED and fire at the end; (6) the closure guard does not require snapshot rows, because it must keep accepting the owner-written closures of the earlier tests and refuses only closures no writer could make before; the confirm, the only closure writer, writes them and the snapshot tables check them at commit; (7) the confirm refuses any isolation other than READ COMMITTED (plan note 15). No HTTP route yet (slice 11e).

The internal `app.begin_settlement_correction` checks the approver and `financial.approve`, takes the draft lock and the Settlement's draft lock, needs the Settlement closed (55000 otherwise, a conflict), records the CONFIRMED decision and then writes the header; `app.link_settlement_correction_effect` links a record before the writer writes it. A deferred check lets a header commit only with its draft confirmed by the same approver (42501) and at least one effect. The 8e-1 refusal and the 8e-2 refusal let a record through only when it is linked to a correction of the same Settlement confirmed in the same transaction (`app.settlement_correction_linked`), never through a session setting. No variant writer exists yet, so no correction can be written outside tests. Choices: (1) every link is unique: a record is the effect of at most one correction; (2) the context of each linked record is checked by the variant writer that writes it (10b to 10g), not by one table check; whether a wrong-Unit move or a returned Payment may link records of another Lease, as DB-SETTLE-005's context sentence does not allow today, is Q-2026-10-06-37 point 5; the closed Settlement refusals pass only records of the Settlement's own Lease; (3) "the same transaction" is exact: the draft's CONFIRMED decision stores the top-level transaction id (`pg_current_xact_id()`, the same inside an exception block) in its result, and the effect check, the link check and the deferred check compare it with the current one and also need the decision written after the current transaction started (review round 2: after a logical restore into a new cluster a stored transaction id can be handed out again) (review round 1, blocker B1: the first build compared the header time with the transaction start, which under READ COMMITTED let a transaction that started earlier treat another's committed correction as its own; a header column would also work but would change DB-SETTLE-003); (4) no time limit is tested by checking that the header's only time checks are "not before the closure" and "not later than the clock plus 5 seconds" (every writer stamps the database clock, so "years after closure" cannot be run); (5) the shared step does not replay: each variant writer replays an exact repeat before calling it (the draft is then already decided, 55000); (6) a variant writer sets no constraint IMMEDIATE before every linked record is written, so it writes its own records instead of calling functions that set `ALL IMMEDIATE` (for example `app.reverse_credit_application`).

Staff record it under `final_settlements.prepare` with a reason (`app.record_settlement_charge_reduction_draft`, `SettlementCorrectionService.record_charge_reduction`); only a `financial.approve` holder confirms it (`app.confirm_settlement_charge_reduction`), which in one transaction records the decision and the correction header (10a) and writes, linked before it is written, a credit Adjustment of the wrong Invoice line on that Invoice's Customer (BR-INV-045). Q-39 (1): yes; a new append-only table `settlement_correction_refund_details`, like 8d's `final_settlement_refund_details`, keeps each Refund a correction pays, so one correction can pay several Refunds, each with its own method, reference note and recipient, and Staff never split a correction by hand; docs/004 gains the table. Q-39 (2): approved tightening: the one-call reversal of the leftover ordinary Credit application, written when a `REFUND` correction releases only part of a Settlement Credit application, is refused; it is still money the closed Settlement relied on (owner answers to Q-2026-10-06-32 and Q-2026-10-06-36). - **V1-056 sub-slice 10c-1b, post-settlement Refund of a paid wrong charge (BR-SETTLE-013, BR-SETTLE-012, BR-CREDIT-014, BR-CREDIT-008, BR-REFUND-014, BR-INV-045, BR-AUTH-010; DB-SETTLE-003, DB-SETTLE-005, DB-REFUND-001; owner answer 1 to Q-2026-10-06-36 and the owner answers to Q-2026-10-07-39; migration `20261104_100`):** a wrong charge that was paid at closure is fixed by a `REFUND` correction. Staff record it under `final_settlements.prepare` with a reason, one Invoice line, the amount, a Refund method and a reference note (`app.record_settlement_refund_draft`, `SettlementCorrectionService.record_refund`); only a `financial.approve` holder confirms it (`app.confirm_settlement_refund`), which in one transaction records the decision and the correction header (10a) and writes, each linked before it is written, the release of the paid part as a credit Adjustment releases it (migration 67, newest first), the credit Adjustment, and one Credit Refund per released source to that Credit's Customer, each with its own `settlement_correction_refund_details` row. Choices: (1) the draft holds one method and one note (Q-39 option (a)); every Refund of the correction keeps them in its own details row, and the Refund row carries the recipient; every released value belongs to the Invoice Customer (BR-CREDIT-014 for a released allocation, BR-CREDIT-008 for a Credit application's Credit), so all Refunds of one correction go to that Customer; (2) the amount is at most the line's charge and must release paid value: removing only unpaid value is a `CHARGE_REDUCTION` (55000), and an unpaid part of the amount is removed with the release (design note); (3) one Refund per released source, not per Credit, so each Refund matches one release record; (4) the draft stores the sources it will release and the source revision covers the line and every source that pays it; any change is stale (P5S02) and the draft stays pending; an unknown or inactive Refund method is a conflict (55000) at record and at confirm, as the Final Settlement draft; (5) the writer writes the release itself instead of calling the migration 67 functions, because those give fresh ids inside and a Settlement Credit application's reversal passes the 8e-2 refusal only when linked first; the release records keep the migration 67 reason and authorization references (`payments.allocations.reverse`, `credits.applications.reverse`, `payments.allocate`, `credits.apply`, `credits.recognize`), which those tables' checks fix; the Adjustment is authorized under `financial.approve` (10c-1a choice 4); (6) the Refund row records `refunds.create` with `processed_by` the approver, as every confirmed Refund draft, and a time after its Credit's latest event; (7) lock order: the draft lock, the Settlement's draft lock, each source Payment and then each source Credit in id order (the order of the allocation, Credit and Refund writers), the Invoice, then the Settlement row; (8) the released Credits have no DB-SETTLE-005 link: the linked Adjustment's `invoice_credit_excess_releases` rows name them; (9) the Refund correction paths (a verified return and its reversal) stay open for these Credit Refunds as for any Credit Refund: a returned Refund puts the value back on the Credit, not on the Settlement's obligations; (10) the approved tightening of Q-39 answer 2 is a new trigger (`a0_customer_credit_application_reversals_settlement_remainder`), not a change of the 8e-2 function, with the 8e-2 SQLSTATE and message; it walks back through every earlier re-post. Relaxing patches: the general Refund source check and the deferred `refunds_credit_customer_confirmed` check also accept the correction's own Credit Refund to a Customer other than the payer (`app.settlement_correction_refund_allowed`). New check named for the owner (10b answer 2): only the approved remainder refusal; it refuses nothing staff can do today, because a re-posted remainder of a Settlement Credit application exists only through a correction. An Invoice that a Deposit application paid stays refused until 10c-2.

- **Owner answers to Q-2026-10-07-41 (2026-10-07), a Refund of a Deposit-paid charge after closure (V1-056 sub-slice 10c-2):** (1) option (a): Deposit value that a correction releases first pays this Lease's open debt through Deposit applications linked to the correction, and only the rest is refunded; it follows every Settlement rule already given: Customer Credit before Deposits (Q-2026-10-05-29), the Security Deposit before the remaining Pet Deposit (Q-2026-10-05-30), the Pet Deposit choice rules (Q-2026-10-05-20, Q-2026-10-05-25) and the kept-Deposit cases (Q-2026-10-05-24); the step is built once and reused by 10d (`FORFEITURE_REVERSAL`); if these rules conflict, the work stops and asks the owner. (2) Yes: the release takes the newest records first across Deposit applications, Payment allocations and Credit applications, as migration 67 does. (3) Yes: `settlement_correction_refund_details` gains two nullable columns (`deposit_id`, `signer_agreement`), docs/004 is updated, and the 8d Deposit Refund source check is relaxed only for a confirmed correction's own Refund, with a test that it accepts nothing else. (4) Yes, with one change: the new Refund in a returned-Refund correction is optional; if the Customer cannot be reached yet, the correction records the verified return only, and the returned amount stays as that Customer's Credit until a later correction refunds it; both the one-call return and its one-call reversal stay refused for a correction's Refund; if this does not fit the design, the work stops and asks the owner.
- **V1-056 sub-slice 10c-2a-1, Deposit application reversals (BR-SETTLE-013, BR-SETTLE-012, BR-SETTLE-009, BR-LEDGER-003, BR-AUTH-010; DB-DEP-006, DB-SETTLE-005, DB-DER-004, DB-DER-010; owner answer 2 to Q-2026-10-06-36; migration `20261105_101`):** the append-only table `app.deposit_application_reversals` (DB-DEP-006) records the reversal of a Final Settlement Deposit application, written only inside a post-settlement correction of the application's Settlement confirmed in the same transaction, by that correction's approver under `financial.approve` (BEFORE INSERT check, 23514), with the Deposit and target locks and the chronology of the Deposit application (later than the latest event of the target and of the Deposit, not before the closure or the correction; review round 1); no role may read or write it, and no writer exists yet (10c-2a-3 and 10e write it). DB-SETTLE-005 gains the link `deposit_application_reversal_id`. Every reader counts only applications not reversed: the Deposit held balance and snapshot, the Invoice line value paid by Deposits as of a time, the Late-payment Charge application summary and the 8a-1 refusal of changes to a Deposit-paid obligation; the latest event time of an allocation target counts the reversal. The Customer Ledger shows `DEPOSIT_APPLICATION_REVERSED` (order 76, the two `DEPOSIT_APPLIED` components with the opposite effect) and the Deposit history shows `APPLICATION_REVERSAL_INVOICE_LINE` or `APPLICATION_REVERSAL_LATE_PAYMENT_CHARGE`. New check named for the owner (10b answer 2): only the BEFORE INSERT check of the new table, which refuses nothing anyone could do before. Review round 1 (independent and security): no blocker; the should-fix findings (the reversal's locks and chronology, an untested Late-payment Charge branch of the relaxed 8a-1 refusal, the list of later writers) are fixed, with tests. Round 2: one should-fix (the target-bound test was masked by the correction bound), fixed. Round 3 (independent and security): no blocker and no should-fix, so 10c-2a-1 is committed under the standing round-3 rule.

- **Owner answers to Q-2026-10-07-42 (2026-10-07), Customer Credit before Deposits after closure and a returned Deposit Refund (V1-056 sub-slices 10c-2a-2, 10c-2a-3 and 10c-2b):** (1) yes, option (a): before released Deposit value pays open debt, the correction first applies each Customer's own Credit to that Customer's own open debt on this Lease, as the Settlement draft does (owner answer 2 to Q-2026-10-05-29); Credit never pays another Customer's debt; the correction writes these Credit applications itself, linked to the correction and recorded as Credit applications of that Settlement (so their one-call reversal is refused, as sub-slice 8e-2), following BR-CREDIT-006, and reuses the 8e-2 Credit application writer with a correction link if it can. (2) Yes, option (a), an approved change of the committed sub-slice 10c-1b: every `REFUND` correction first uses the Credit it releases against that Credit's own Customer's open debt on this Lease and refunds only the rest; a Customer with no open debt on this Lease (for example a third-party payer) gets the Refund as today; 10c-1b is changed in sub-slice 10c-2a-3, with tests for both cases. (3) Yes, option (a): a returned Deposit Refund goes back to the Deposit, not to Customer Credit; the returned amount stays held by the Deposit until a later correction, which first pays this Lease's open debt in the DL-032 order and then refunds the rest; the owner answer 4 to Q-2026-10-07-41 (the returned amount stays as that Customer's Credit) applies to a returned Credit Refund only.
- **V1-056 sub-slice 10c-2a-2, the shared DL-032 step after closure (DL-032, BR-SETTLE-004, BR-SETTLE-005, BR-SETTLE-006, BR-SETTLE-008, BR-SETTLE-013, BR-SETTLE-017, BR-CREDIT-006, BR-CREDIT-008, BR-CREDIT-014, BR-DEP-027, BR-REFUND-014, BR-REFUND-015, BR-AUTH-010; owner answers 1 and 3 to Q-2026-10-07-41 and 1 and 2 to Q-2026-10-07-42; migration `20261106_102`):** value a post-settlement correction releases, or a Deposit holds again after closure, is used under the Settlement rules before anything is refunded. A correction draft that runs the step keeps `plan` (the Settlement plan format), `plan_overlay` (what the correction itself changes before the step) and `plan_result`; the internal check `app.settlement_correction_plan_result` reads the closed Settlement as the Settlement preview does with the overlay applied, and the internal `app.post_settlement_correction_plan` runs inside the correction after the variant's release: the check again on the real state (a different result is stale, P5S02), then the Customer Credit applications (the 8e-2 writer with a correction link), the Deposit applications and the Deposit Refunds, each linked to the correction before it is written with a fresh id. The 8e-2 Credit application checks, the Deposit application check and the 8d Deposit Refund source check accept a correction's own record only (relaxing); `settlement_correction_refund_details` gains `deposit_id` and `signer_agreement`. No variant uses the step yet (10c-2a-3, 10c-2b and 10d will), so no role can reach it. Choices: (1) the plan has the Settlement plan's format and checks (copied, not shared: the 8c check needs a ready preview and an open Settlement, and is not changed); (2) the overlay lets a variant record the draft before its release; a Deposit in the overlay counts as following DL-032 because the variant's release guarantees it, and the confirm checks the real state; (3) of the preview's blocking issues only a waiting draft on a Settlement source refuses the step (the 8r rule and the Settlement's pending-draft rule); the other issues describe the closure, which the 8e-1 refusals keep unchanged; (4) the step covers every DL-032 Deposit that holds money, not only the one the correction releases (BR-SETTLE-008: every remaining Deposit balance is applied or refunded; owner answer 3 to Q-2026-10-07-42: a later correction pays the debt and refunds the rest of a returned amount); (5) Customer Credit before Deposits (Q-42 answer 1, "before released Deposit value pays open debt") applies only when a Deposit holds money; this differs from the Settlement draft, where each Customer's Credit must pay that Customer's open debt even when no Deposit pays (owner answer 2 to Q-2026-10-05-29), because an unconditional rule would force a Credit-only correction to apply the Credit of Customers it does not concern, beyond Q-42 answer 2 (named for the owner after review round 1); released Credit pays its own Customer's open debt on the Lease before any Refund (Q-42 answer 2) applies to each Credit the overlay names, whether or not a Deposit holds money, and it counts all of that Credit's available value, also value it held before the correction (named for the owner after review round 1); (6) one Refund method, note, recipient and agreement per correction plan (owner answer 3 to Q-2026-10-07-41, as the method and note of 10c-1b); (7) the 8e-2 writer is reused (owner answer 1 to Q-42): it reads a correction's step from its `plan`, resolves the Credit key through `app.settlement_correction_credit_id` (a key may name a Payment allocation the correction releases, whose value becomes the Invoice Customer's Credit, BR-CREDIT-014) and gives the record a fresh id linked to the correction (sub-slice 10b rule); its Settlement path is unchanged; (8) a correction's Deposit application takes the Settlement's next order number, and its stage order is checked within the correction; (9) a correction's Deposit Refund records `financial.approve` as a Settlement Deposit Refund does; (10) the step defers its own link keys again, because an earlier writer in the same transaction may have set every constraint IMMEDIATE (full run P1); (11) the receipt reversal recorder is not changed: a waiting correction draft is protected by the pending-draft rule at the step and by the stale check, so no tightening is needed; (12, review round 1) a correction's Deposit application must match a Deposit step of the correction's plan (Deposit, stage, target and amount), each step at most once, as its Credit applications and Deposit Refunds do; (13, review round 1) `settlement_correction_refund_details` is unique on the correction and the Deposit (each Deposit refunded at most once per correction, as 8d once per Settlement), and its deferred check also needs the details to name the Refund's own Deposit, and no Deposit for a Credit Refund; (14, review round 1) the step itself checks READ COMMITTED and takes its locks again (held already when the variant took them), and the lock order is the Settlement confirm's: the draft and Settlement draft locks, the Lease row `FOR UPDATE` (added after review round 2, owner answer to Q-2026-10-07-43: the move-out inspection command that supersedes an inspection locks the same row `FOR UPDATE`, so no line stops being pet damage while the step runs), the steps' Payments and Credits, the Lease's Charges and Invoices, the Settlement row, then the Deposits; (15, review round 1) the step compares the whole recorded result; (16, review round 1, accepted race) the Credit-before-Deposits rule reads every available Credit of the Lease's Customers but locks only the Credits the steps name (as the Settlement confirm): a Credit recognized by a concurrent one-call command after the step's check is not used first; nothing is overpaid. New checks named for the owner (10b answer 2): none refuses anything anyone could do before; the relaxed checks still refuse every record that is not a correction's own.

- **Owner answers to Q-2026-10-07-43 (2026-10-07), sub-slice 10c-2a-2 after review round 2:** option (a), as an owner exception like Q-2026-10-05-31 and Q-2026-10-07-40: (1) the step must hold a lock that really stops the move-out inspection from being superseded while it runs; the command that supersedes an inspection (`app.move_out_inspection_record`, and its insert trigger) locks the Lease row `FOR UPDATE` and the step's lock function did not, so the step now locks the Lease row `FOR UPDATE` right after the two draft locks, as the Settlement confirm (the lock order of the 8e-3 plan note), with a test that an inspection correction waits while the step runs and that the Pet Deposit cannot pay a line that is no longer pet damage; (2) tests of the step's two guards inside a live correction (a person other than the approver; the READ COMMITTED refusal); (3) tests of the BR-DEP-027 branches (the staff reason refused at an unpaid-Initial termination; a Pet Deposit Refund while other debt stays open, accepted by the plan check and the Deposit Refund source check) and the BR-CREDIT-006 branches (the Rent-first refusal; the proposal and designation bases the correction's Credit check requires); then the backend unit suite and the full PostgreSQL suite once each, one more independent and security round on the three fixes and the code they touch, and the commit only if that round has no blocker and no should-fix. - **Known limit (V1-056 sub-slice 10c-2a-2, owner answer to Q-2026-10-07-43):** the Credit-before-Deposits rule of the post-settlement correction step reads every available Credit of the Lease's Customers but locks only the Credits its steps name, as the Settlement confirm does. A Credit recognized by another one-call command right after the step's check is not used first. Nothing is overpaid, and that Credit stays with the Customer.

The release takes whole sources newest first across Deposit applications, Payment allocations and Credit applications, only until the paid part is covered (Q-41 answer 2); a released Deposit application is reversed whole (sub-slice 10c-2a-1) and its value goes back to its Deposit, never to Customer Credit; the rest of a partly released Deposit application is paid again only as a step of the correction's plan; the re-posted rests of Payment allocations and Credit applications keep every other line's amounts, so no other already-paid line changes how it is paid. Every `REFUND` correction then runs the shared DL-032 step of sub-slice 10c-2a-2: the draft request carries `plan` (staff choose every step; every Deposit Refund step uses the draft's method and note), the recorder builds the overlay of its own release and stores the check's result, and the confirm writes the release, runs the step (Credit first, Deposit applications, Deposit Refunds) and only then writes one Credit Refund per released Payment allocation or Credit application for the value left in that Credit, at most what the correction released to it (Q-42 answer 2: a Customer with open debt on the Lease gets back only the rest; a Customer with none gets the Refund as before; a correction may end with no Refund). The confirm takes the Lease row `FOR UPDATE` right after the two draft locks, before the source Payments, in the 8e-3 order (Q-44 answer 4). A remaining Pet Deposit step with the Customer's choice needs a choice text other than the one recorded at the Settlement (Q-44 answer 3); at the BR-DEP-027 terminations the step still refuses the staff basis. Relaxing (Q-46): the 8a-1 refusal of an Invoice Adjustment lets through only an Adjustment linked to a correction of its Invoice's own closed Settlement, confirmed in the same transaction by that correction's approver under `financial.approve` (internal `app.settlement_correction_adjustment_allowed`); every unlinked Adjustment stays refused. No new check was needed for "no line paid more than its new amount": `app.validate_invoice_adjustment_effect` already refuses at commit a line whose outstanding value at the Adjustment's time, Deposit applications not reversed included, is below zero (a test shows it on the new path). Choices: (1) the release reads one list of sources ordered by their recorded time, newest first, with the source id as the tie-break; (2) a Deposit application is never split: it is reversed whole and its unreleased rest is a plain open obligation for the step, so staff choose where the Deposit value goes under the Settlement rules (Credit first; DL-032 order); (3) the empty plan is valid only when the step has nothing to pay (no Deposit holds money and no released Credit's Customer owes on the Lease), as 10c-1b behaved; otherwise the step refuses the draft (55000); (4) the `CHARGE_REDUCTION` recorder (10c-1a) still refuses a Deposit-paid Invoice; (5, review rounds 1 and 2, security) after the draft locks and the Lease row the confirm takes every other lock through the step's lock function (except the Refund method, `FOR SHARE`, last, as sub-slice 8d and the step take it), which for a `REFUND` draft (patched in migration `20261107_103`, same signature) takes the released sources' Payments and Credits in its single id-ordered Payment and Credit passes together with the Credit steps' (a separate pass could lock Payments out of id order and deadlock with another Lease's correction or Settlement confirm that names a Credit of the same Customer) and the corrected Invoice `FOR UPDATE` in its id-ordered Invoice pass after the Late-payment Charges (an Invoice locked before the Charges could deadlock with a one-call writer that locks a Charge and then its source Invoice); the comment before the lock function in migration `20261106_102` ("then its own sources ... then calls this") is a historical migration and is not edited; (6, review round 1) a remaining Pet Deposit choice is also refused when its text equals the choice of an earlier confirmed correction of the same Settlement (one agreement per correction); known limits for the owner: the database compares the recorded text only, so a changed text passes and the staff remain responsible for recording a real new choice; the comparison runs when the draft is recorded, not again at confirm (a second draft recorded with the same text before the first is confirmed becomes stale once the first correction's Pet Deposit step changes the Settlement's open total and closing balances, P5S02, and is then recorded and checked again); (7, review round 1, answered) the Q-46 exception does not check the Adjustment type or the correction kind: owner answer to Q-46 lets through any Adjustment linked to a confirmed correction of the Invoice's own Settlement, only the `REFUND` correction reaches it today (the `CHARGE_REDUCTION` recorder refuses a Deposit-paid Invoice, `EXTRA_CHARGE` writes no Adjustment), a debit Adjustment of a paid line stays refused (BR-INV-044), and each later correction kind states in its own design whether it relies on it; (8, review round 1, answered) a `REFUND` draft recorded before migration `20261107_103` has no `plan`; its confirm fails with 22023 and writes nothing; no persistent database holds such a draft (V1-056 is unpublished). New checks named for the owner (10b answer 2): none refuses anything anyone could do before, except the approved change of Q-42 answer 2 (a `REFUND` correction whose released Credit's Customer still owes on the Lease needs a plan that pays that debt first).

- **Owner answer to Q-2026-10-08-49 (2026-10-08), inspection supersede after closure (V1-056 sub-slice 10c-2a-4):** option (a). (1) Once a Lease's Final Settlement is closed, every supersede of a move-out inspection on that Lease is refused; the refusal is a conflict, like the other refusals after closure. (2) Damage found after closure is recorded as a new, separate inspection that supersedes nothing; the inspection the closed Settlement relied on never changes. (3) A wrong finding on the inspection the Settlement relied on is fixed only with a post-settlement correction (sub-slice 10c-2a-5 for a wrong pet classification). (4) Known limit: a mistake in an inspection recorded after closure cannot be fixed by a supersede either. The wrong finding is simply not billed, because billing it still needs an `EXTRA_CHARGE` correction confirmed by a `financial.approve` holder. (5) Before code, a read-only check that nothing assumes one chain of inspections per Lease, in particular the readers that decide current findings and pet damage for the Settlement and for corrections; if one does, the question goes to the owner and the work stops. Done 2026-10-08, none found: "current" is decided per inspection (an inspection that no other inspection supersedes) by the Damage source check (migration 65), `app.invoice_line_is_pet_damage` (migration 86; used by the Settlement preview, the Settlement Deposit Refund source, the Settlement correction plan check and step, migrations 89, 91 and 102), the extra charge plan and source state (migration 98) and the inspection snapshot and page read (migration 60); the inspection service and the frontend pass only inspection and finding ids. (6) The committed 10b test `test_a_damage_extra_charge_bills_a_current_unbilled_finding_and_a_stale_draft_waits` changes its set-up so that the damage found after closure is a separate inspection; it keeps its name and must still prove the same behaviour; a part that can no longer happen after closure is named here and in the report; the independent reviewer compares it with its version at HEAD and confirms it was not weakened.

Known limit (owner answer to Q-49, point 4): an inspection recorded after closure cannot be superseded either; its wrong finding is simply not billed, because billing it needs an `EXTRA_CHARGE` correction confirmed by a `financial.approve` holder.

- **Owner answer to Q-2026-10-08-51 (2026-10-08), a supersede in a REPEATABLE READ transaction (V1-056 sub-slice 10c-2a-4, review round 1):** option (a); the further tightening is approved. Any inspection supersede outside READ COMMITTED is refused with 55000, before and after closure, as the Settlement confirm and the correction confirms already require. Reason (both round-1 reviewers): a REPEATABLE READ or SERIALIZABLE transaction whose snapshot is older than the Settlement's start does not see the Settlement row, so the closed-Settlement read finds nothing and the Lease row lock raises nothing (the start and the confirm lock the Lease row but never change it); the design's "at REPEATABLE READ the row lock fails with 40001" held only when the Settlement row was in the snapshot. No screen or service path changes (the service always writes at READ COMMITTED); an existing test that supersedes outside READ COMMITTED changes only that expectation and is named in the report; a new test covers the gap itself (a REPEATABLE READ transaction that started before the Settlement existed is refused when it tries the supersede after closure); the design note is corrected.

Only a Deposit on the DL-032 path may be refunded so (55000 otherwise; Q-2026-10-09-61 stays open for the others). Also after review round 1: a Deposit correction's draft records the Deposit's owner, and its audit event names the recipient of the Deposit Refund the step wrote, or the Deposit's owner when nothing was refunded; one correction may still carry two Refund recipients (the Credit's Customer and a Deposit Refund to an agreed Signer), as `REFUND_RETURN`; the new Refund's method and note are required even when nothing is refunded, as the `REFUND` correction; the human-approver check of the confirm is defence in depth (a service identity is refused first, P4506), as in the other variants.

- **Owner answers to Q-2026-10-09-63 (2026-10-09), the refund-only form after review round 1 (V1-056 sub-slice 10c-2b-3):** (1) Option (a): a `HELD_VALUE_REFUND` correction may name an earlier return-only `REFUND_RETURN` correction only while that correction still has value left; it is checked at record (55000, "Nothing the earlier correction returned is left to refund"); at the confirm a draft whose earlier correction's value changed after it was recorded is stale (P5S02, its source digest holds the value left, the Credit's or Deposit's value and the linked corrections) and stays pending, and the same check runs again as a backstop; naming the same correction again after its value is gone changes no money and no record. How the value left is counted (never below 0): for a Credit, the earlier correction's verified return to that Credit, less the Credit applications from that Credit written by the earlier correction's own step and by every confirmed `HELD_VALUE_REFUND` correction linked to it, and less the Refunds from that Credit of those linked corrections; at the confirm this correction's own step applications and Refund are left out, so they do not lower the cap of its own Refund (answer 2); the Credit must also still hold value (55000, "The Credit holds no returned value to refund", also when the plan has other steps). For a Deposit, the earlier correction's verified return to that Deposit, less the Deposit applications and the Refunds from that Deposit written by every confirmed `HELD_VALUE_REFUND` correction linked to it (a return-only Deposit correction runs no step); the Deposit must also still hold money. Only records of corrections linked to the named correction lower its value: Deposit money that another correction's step settles (a held-value correction linked to another earlier correction, or a `REFUND` or `REFUND_RETURN` correction with a new Refund, each of which must apply or refund every held DL-032 Deposit balance, BR-SETTLE-008) lowers only what the Deposit holds, and the audit event of the correction that settled it lists every Deposit balance it settled. (2) Kept as built, as approved for sub-slice 10c-2b-1 (docs/010 choice (1)): Credit spent through the ordinary Credit paths (a one-call Credit application, an ordinary Credit Refund draft) lowers only the Credit's available value, and the available value still caps every Refund. **Known limit:** the value an earlier correction left can be more than the Customer can still get back (in a Credit for value spent through the ordinary Credit paths, and, by the counting of answer 1, in a Deposit for money another correction settled); no Refund is ever more than the Credit or the Deposit holds. Updated by sub-slice 10c-2b-4 (owner answer to Q-2026-10-09-64): a held-value correction now uses, in each Deposit, only what its own earlier correction left there, so in a Deposit this limit stays only for money that a correction naming no earlier correction settled (see the 10c-2b-4 entry); the Credit part is unchanged.

- **V1-056 sub-slice 10c-2b-4, the stricter Deposit count of the refund-only form (BR-SETTLE-008, BR-SETTLE-013, DL-032, BR-AUTH-010; owner answer to Q-2026-10-09-64; migration `20261116_112`):** a `HELD_VALUE_REFUND` correction uses, in each Deposit, at most what its earlier correction left there (`app.settlement_held_deposit_value`), the Lease debt it pays and the Refund together. A Deposit the earlier correction returned nothing to gives it nothing: a Credit correction (its earlier correction returned a Credit Refund) uses no Deposit money, and Deposit money that another earlier correction returned stays held until staff prepare a correction that names that correction. As built after owner answer 1 to Q-2026-10-09-65 (option (b), "at most"): the correction may leave part of the value its earlier correction left in the Deposit; that part stays held for a later correction that names the same earlier correction; but a correction whose limit reaches held money must use some of it. BR-SETTLE-008 and the DL-032 order stay as they are for every correction, also one that leaves value held (for example no Deposit Refund while debt the Deposit could pay stays open). Refusals (55000): more than the limit in any Deposit, "A held-value correction uses at most what its earlier correction left in each Deposit"; none of that value used, the existing message "Every remaining Deposit balance must be applied or refunded" (kept, so the committed no-plan refusal of the Deposit form is unchanged). (Before the owner answer the correction had to use exactly the smaller of the value left and what the Deposit holds; review round 2 found a case where two corrections then each stay refused.) This replaces, for this variant, choice (2) of sub-slice 10c-2b-3: a held-value correction no longer applies or refunds every held DL-032 Deposit balance, and a Credit correction no longer settles held Deposit money (which owner answer 2 to Q-2026-10-08-59 had allowed). Built as exact-text patches of four functions (no new function, table or column; no service change): the shared plan check takes an optional overlay key `held_left` (a Deposit id to cents; malformed, or together with `hold_deposits` true, 22023) and checks the limit in place of the every-balance rule; the recorder stores it in the draft's `plan_overlay` (`{Deposit: value left}` for the Deposit form, `{}` for the Credit form); the shared step passes it for this variant (a draft without it: `{}`, no Deposit money); the confirm treats a draft whose stored limit differs from the recomputed one as stale (P5S02), so a draft recorded under `20261114_110` stays pending. The other step rules stay (DL-032 order, Credit before Deposits, pet damage first, no Deposit Refund while debt the Deposit could pay stays open, the Security Deposit before the remaining Pet Deposit). Because other held money is no longer used in the same correction, these rules now order the corrections: while the Security Deposit holds money, a correction limited to the Pet Deposit cannot use the remaining Pet Deposit (step 5) for other debt; and, added after review round 1 (the security reviewer's finding), while a Pet Deposit keeps held money that the correction may not use and pet damage stays open after the Pet Deposit's step, no Security Deposit step pays that pet damage (55000, "The Pet Deposit pays open pet damage before any other use or Refund"; narrowed after review round 2 so that the Security Deposit may still pay other debt; owner answer 2 to Q-2026-10-09-65: owner answer 3 (ii) to Q-2026-10-05-20 and the 10c-2b-2a hold rule only stop the Security Deposit from paying pet damage instead of the Pet Deposit, and never stopped it from paying other debt), so the correction that names the Pet Deposit's earlier correction pays it; a Security Deposit Refund while that debt stays open is refused by the existing rule. Pet damage paid by the Pet Deposit itself (step 3) and a Pet Refund where the rules allow it are not held back. The case of Q-2026-10-09-65 (both Deposits hold other corrections' money, pet damage and other debt open) is settled through several corrections in either order, because a correction may leave part of its value held. Each Customer's Credit still pays that Customer's open debt first whenever any Deposit holds money, also money this correction may not use. **Known limit, updated (owner instruction):** the value a return-only correction left in a Deposit can still be more than the Deposit holds, but only when a correction that names no earlier correction settled that money: a `REFUND` correction, a `REFUND_RETURN` correction with a new Refund and a `PET_DAMAGE_RECLASSIFICATION` correction still apply or refund every held DL-032 Deposit balance (BR-SETTLE-008), and a return-only Credit correction still applies held Deposit money that open debt can take (owner answer 2 to Q-2026-10-08-59). Naming that earlier correction is then refused (55000, "The Deposit holds no returned money to refund"). After review round 1: when such a correction settled the money and a later return-only correction brings money back to the same Deposit, a correction that names the first one may use the new money (the smaller of its value left and what the Deposit holds), and naming the later one is then refused for the same reason. The settled money is a linked effect of the correction that settled it; no Refund is ever more than the Deposit holds. **Owner check, the Credit side (reported, not changed):** the Credit form does not count the debt it pays in the same way. Its new Refund is at most what the earlier correction left, but this held-value correction's own step applications from the Credit are left out of that cap (owner answer 2 to Q-2026-10-09-63, kept as built), so the debt it pays and its Refund together may exceed what the earlier correction left (the committed test `test_a_held_credit_first_pays_its_customer_s_debt_and_only_the_rest_is_refunded`: 1,800 left, 1,500 paid to debt and 500 refunded); what the earlier correction left is lowered only by its own step's applications from the Credit and by the applications and Refunds of the other corrections linked to it. Owner answer 3 to Q-2026-10-09-65: kept as built, because a Customer's Credit pays that Customer's own debt first, whatever its source (owner answers to Q-2026-10-05-29 and Q-2026-10-08-55). **Known limit, Credit side (owner answer 3):** a held-value correction's own Refund counts against the value its earlier correction left, but the debt that correction pays from the Credit does not; the debt paid by the earlier correction's own step and by the held-value corrections confirmed before it does lower what is left for later corrections.

Staff record it under `final_settlements.prepare` with a reason, the Charge, the amount, a Refund method, a reference note and the DL-032 plan (`app.record_settlement_late_charge_refund_draft`, `SettlementCorrectionService.record_late_charge_refund`; the draft's `target_kind` is `LATE_PAYMENT_CHARGE` and its `refund` object also stores the Charge's source Invoice); only a `financial.approve` holder confirms it (`app.confirm_settlement_late_charge_refund`, `confirm_late_charge_refund`; human approver, READ COMMITTED, stale P5S02, replay). In one transaction the confirm reverses whole sources newest first until the paid part is covered (Q-41 answer 2), writes one linked Late-payment Charge correction (`REDUCTION`, or `CHARGE_REVERSAL` for the whole current obligation, the 10c-3a rule), re-posts each reversed source's unreleased rest to the same Charge, recognizes released Payment value as Credit of the Charge's Customer (BR-CREDIT-014, also when that Customer did not pay) and gives released Credit value back to its Credit, runs the shared DL-032 step (released Credit first pays its own Customer's open debt on the Lease, Q-42 answer 2) and pays one Credit Refund per released source of what is left in its Credit, at most what was released to it, to that Credit's Customer with the draft's method and note. Refused at record (and, after a change, stale at the confirm): an open Settlement (55000); a Charge not of the Settlement's Lease (P0002); a reversed Charge or one on a VOID Invoice (55000); a Charge a Deposit application paid (55000, until sub-slice 10c-3b-2); more than the current obligation (55000, "The Refund correction exceeds the Late-payment Charge"); an amount that releases no paid value (55000, the Invoice-line message: that is a `CHARGE_REDUCTION`); an inactive Refund method (55000). The Invoice-line `REFUND` confirm now refuses a draft with a `target_kind` (not found), on the replay path and the main path, and the Charge confirm refuses an Invoice-line draft. **The release record (owner answer 2 to Q-2026-10-09-66, a technical choice):** `app.invoice_credit_excess_releases` is relaxed, never rebuilt: `invoice_adjustment_id` becomes nullable and a new nullable `late_payment_charge_correction_id` (FK, ON DELETE RESTRICT, indexed) is added; a release row names exactly one of the two, the reason "Invoice adjustment credit excess" with an Adjustment or "Late-payment Charge correction credit excess" with a Charge correction; every existing row keeps its Adjustment. Every money movement links to the correction: the reversals, the Charge correction, the re-posted rests and the Refunds are DB-SETTLE-005 effects, each release row names the Charge correction and the released Credit names its release row. Patched readers (exact-text patches, owner, SECURITY DEFINER, settings and grants kept): the release validator (a Charge branch: the reversed source targets that Charge with the same reason, the release at most what it applied), the Credit recognition validator (finds the Charge's Customer through the Charge correction), the relaxed Credit Refund check and the plan's Credit key (join the release rows through the Charge correction effect too), the two audit labels of re-posted allocations and Credit applications (the release row's reason), the lock function (a Charge `REFUND` draft adds its Charge to the Charge pass FOR UPDATE; its source Invoice joins the Invoice pass through the `refund` object) and, approved under Q-2026-10-09-68, the shared plan check's Credit overlay. Choices for the owner: (1) the reversals, the Charge correction, each re-post and each released Credit are stamped after the Charge's latest event (and, for a Credit's record, the Credit's latest event), so the Charge correction follows every allocation and Credit application on the Charge (its serializer; 10c-3a security note 3); (2) the source digest holds the Settlement, the Charge (current obligation, corrections, active applications, VOID state) and every source that pays it with its Credit, as the Invoice-line form; (3) the released Credit's `customer_authorization_reference` is `late-payment-charge-correction:` and the Charge correction id. - **V1-056 sub-slice 10d, a forfeiture reversal after closure (BR-SETTLE-013, BR-SETTLE-008, BR-SETTLE-016, BR-DEP-019, BR-DEP-022, BR-DEP-023, BR-DEP-026, DL-032, BR-REFUND-014, BR-REFUND-015, BR-CREDIT-006, BR-AUTH-010; owner answer 4 to Q-2026-10-06-36, answer 1 to Q-2026-10-06-37, answers 1 and 3 to Q-2026-10-07-41, answers 1 to 3 to Q-2026-10-07-42, Q-2026-10-05-24, Q-2026-10-10-71; migration `20261119_115`):** the post-settlement correction variant `FORFEITURE_REVERSAL` reverses a confirmed Lease Deposit forfeiture of a Deposit of the Settlement's Lease once the Settlement is closed. Staff record it under `final_settlements.prepare` with a reason, the forfeiture, an evidence reference, the correction's Refund method and reference note and the DL-032 plan (`app.record_settlement_forfeiture_reversal_draft`, `SettlementCorrectionService.record_forfeiture_reversal`); only a `financial.approve` holder confirms it (`app.confirm_settlement_forfeiture_reversal`, `confirm_forfeiture_reversal`; human approver, READ COMMITTED, stale P5S02 with the draft left pending, replay). In one transaction the confirm takes the 8e-3 locks (the draft lock, the Settlement's draft lock, the Lease row, the shared lock function with every Deposit of the Lease, then the forfeiture row), checks the source digest and the recorder's check again, takes the Refund methods FOR SHARE, writes the decision and the header, links and writes the forfeiture reversal through the existing reversal function (the approver as actor, `deposits.correct`, the draft's reason and evidence reference, the command record keyed by the draft and the `deposit.disposition.reversed` audit event, as the 6b confirm writes it), and runs the shared DL-032 step on the real state: each Customer's Credit first pays that Customer's own open debt (Q-42 answer 1), the Deposit pays the Lease's open debt in the DL-032 order and only the rest is refunded to the Primary Tenant or an agreed signed Signer (BR-SETTLE-008, BR-REFUND-015); a correction may end with no Refund when the debt takes all of it, and the debt left stays on its Customer's ledger (BR-SETTLE-016). The recorder checks the plan with the forfeited amount added to the Deposit whatever its path; at the confirm the reversal puts the Deposit on the DL-032 path (Q-24) before the step checks the real state against the recorded result. Refused at record: an open Settlement (55000); a forfeiture that is not one of a Deposit of the Settlement's Lease, a Reservation forfeiture or an unknown one (P0002, "Lease Deposit forfeiture was not found"); a forfeiture already reversed (55000); another forfeiture of the same Deposit that stays active (55000, owner answer 2 to Q-2026-10-10-71); an inactive Refund method (55000); a Deposit Refund step with another method or note (22023); a waiting draft on a Settlement source, such as a 6b reversal draft of the forfeiture (55000, the shared check); the plan rules of the shared check. The source digest holds the Settlement, the forfeiture and its reversals, the Deposit (held value, latest balance event, path, the other active forfeitures) and the Deposit's waiting drafts other than correction drafts; so a 6b draft recorded or confirmed after the correction draft makes the correction draft stale at its confirm (P5S02, not the record-time 55000), and a change of debt or Credit makes it stale through the shared step's comparison. Choices for the owner: (1) the reversal row and its audit name the approver and `deposits.correct`, as the 6b confirm does (slice 12 owner item on approver naming); the authority is the linked correction (`final_settlements.prepare` prepares, `financial.approve` confirms) and the correction's audit evidence names `financial.approve`; (2) the reversal row and its audit event are stamped with the confirm's statement time, so they are dated just before the correction's decision and header that link them, as in 6b; reports read them through the link; the reversal audit's resulting state is the Deposit snapshot before the step applies or refunds the money; (3) no new table, column or patch: the existing reversal function, link and shared step serve unchanged. Design test items not built as written: the positive Deposit Refund to another signed Signer with the written agreement (no fixture has a kept Deposit on a Lease with a second signed Signer; owner answer 1 to Q-2026-10-10-71: refusals only now, the positive test in the plan's real-path task before 10h); a pending forfeiture draft of the Deposit (a forfeiture draft cannot be recorded after closure since sub-slice 10c-2b-2a; a pending 6b reversal draft is tested). **Known gap until sub-slice 10h:** the 6b draft still reverses a closed Settlement's forfeiture without the step; 10h closes it (owner answer 6 to Q-2026-10-10-69).

The draft lists every active allocation, every Customer Credit recognized from the Payment with its active applications and every active Deposit receipt. In one transaction the confirm writes the decision and one `app.payment_returns` row, then reverses the Credit applications, the Credits, the allocations and the Deposit receipts and then the Payment; the debt comes back on its obligations and stays with their Customers (BR-SETTLE-016); the Payment row and its Receipt never change. The slice 7 refusals (a moved allocation; a Credit released from a moved allocation) and the sub-slice 8g refusal (a Credit released to a Customer other than the payer) let a reversal of that Payment's record through only while its return is confirmed in the same transaction, so both lasting blocks end. Choices for the owner: (1) each reversal row names the approver and its table's fixed authorization string (`credits.applications.reverse`, `credits.reverse`, `payments.allocations.reverse`, `deposits.correct` for the receipt), as the correction writers do (slice 12 approver-naming item); the Payment reversal row, whose column has no fixed string, names `financial.approve`; the authority is the confirmed draft, recorded in the `payment_returns` row and the audit event; (2) a receipt reversal goes through the existing receipt reversal function and is stamped with the confirm's statement time, as the 8r confirm, so it is dated just before the return row; the result finds it by its command key; (3) a new preparer capability makes eight preparer capabilities, so the two capability-scoped draft reads (`app.financial_draft_resource_by_capability`, `app.list_financial_drafts_by_capability`) accept eight instead of seven (a relaxing exact-text patch; without it every `financial.approve` reader's draft read would be refused); (4) the Settlement preview is not changed: a Settlement may close while a `PAYMENT_RETURN` draft waits; when the closure relies on that Payment's records, the draft is then stale at its confirm (P5S02, the draft stays pending), and staff withdraw it and record the correction instead (as built after review round 1; corrected after review round 2).

(3) Q-72 point 1 detail, confirmed: with no closed Final Settlement, the charge for a Refund already paid out from the returned value is an ordinary one-time Miscellaneous charge on the Lease the money came from, issued in the same confirm; a returned Payment whose Refund has no Lease to charge on is refused (a known limit); `EXTRA_CHARGE` is used only inside a correction of a closed Settlement (sub-slice 10e-1c). (4) Q-75 point 1, option (A): under pay back, the returned money is DL-032 money everywhere, before and after closure; any correction that runs the shared DL-032 step must apply or refund it (BR-SETTLE-008). (5) Q-75 point 2, option (b): any returned Refund that was paid before the termination is paid back, also when it came back before the termination; a forfeiture leaves it out (the Q-73 answer). BR-DEP-022 ("non-refundable according to the signed Lease") keeps what the Deposit held at the termination, read as not including returned Refund money. Implementer note: a Pet Refund-review Refund may be paid again after a return while the Lease is signed, so answer (b) needs a rule for which money such a later Refund pays (Q-2026-10-10-76, open; sub-slice 10c-2b-5 waits for it). (6) Standing instruction: when one sub-slice waits for an owner answer, the next sub-slice that does not depend on that answer may be built without asking; the report says so.
- **V1-056 sub-slice 10e-1b, a returned Payment that a closed Final Settlement relied on (BR-SETTLE-013, BR-SETTLE-016, BR-PAY-042, BR-CREDIT-014, BR-DEP-023, BR-AUTH-010; DB-PAY-009, DB-SETTLE-003, DB-SETTLE-005, DB-DEP-006; owner answers 1 and 5 to Q-2026-10-06-36, answers 2, 3 and 5 to Q-2026-10-06-37, answers (a) to Q-2026-10-10-72 points 2 and 3; migration `20261121_117`):** a bounced Payment whose records a closed Final Settlement relied on is returned by the `RETURNED_PAYMENT` correction of that Settlement: a `final_settlements.prepare` holder records it with a reason and an evidence reference (`app.record_settlement_returned_payment_draft`, `SettlementCorrectionService.record_returned_payment`); only a `financial.approve` holder confirms it (`app.confirm_settlement_returned_payment`, `confirm_returned_payment`; a person, READ COMMITTED, replay, stale P5S02 with the draft left pending). In one transaction the confirm writes the decision, the correction header and the `payment_returns` row naming the correction, then, each linked to the correction before it is written: the reversals of the Payment's Credit applications (a Final Settlement or correction Credit application passes the 8e-2 refusals only by that link), its Credits and its allocations, the reversals of the forfeitures, Deposit applications and receipts of every Deposit it funded, and the Payment reversal. The debt comes back on its obligations and stays with their Customers (BR-SETTLE-016); the Settlement row and its closure snapshots never change. Each funded Deposit ends empty, so there is no DL-032 step; a kept Deposit's forfeiture is reversed in the same correction and no charge is made for the Deposit amount (Q-72 point 2). Refused (55000): a Payment that is not RECEIVED; a Payment this Settlement did not rely on (the correction of the closed Settlement that did, or else the `PAYMENT_RETURN` draft, returns it; corrected after review round 1); a record that another closed Final Settlement also relied on; a Refund paid from the Payment's value that is not fully returned (sub-slice 10e-1c); a funded Deposit's forfeiture governed by another Lease; a funded Deposit's application of another Final Settlement; a funded Deposit that would still hold money after the return; a waiting draft that names the Payment or one of its records. **Known limit (owner answer (a) to Q-2026-10-10-72 point 3):** a Payment whose records two closed Final Settlements relied on cannot be returned in the system: a correction of either Settlement and the `PAYMENT_RETURN` draft refuse it (55000), and staff record the loss outside the system; a multi-Settlement correction is in the plan as possible later work. Choices for the owner: (1) the receipt reversal is written by the correction confirm itself with the same `deposits.correct`, command record and `deposit.receipt.reversed` audit event as the receipt reversal function, because that function stamps the statement time, which would date the receipt reversal before the Deposit application reversals and make the Deposit's history negative (refused); the forfeiture reversal still goes through the existing function (statement time, before the application reversals); (2) the write steps are an internal helper (`app.post_settlement_returned_payment`) for sub-slice 10e-1c to reuse (10e-2 keeps the Payment, so it needs the helper split first; corrected after review round 1); the helper runs no refusal itself, so every caller runs the source and refusal check under the same locks first; the sub-slice 10e-1a confirm is not changed; (3) the lock order is the draft lock, then the Payment's return lock (as the 10e-1a recorder and confirm), then the 8e-3 order (the Settlement's draft lock, the Lease row, the correction lock function, which gains a `RETURNED_PAYMENT` branch and also locks the targets and Deposits that branch adds outside the Lease), then the funded Deposits' forfeitures; (4) relaxing exact-text patch: `app.validate_payment_return` accepts a `RETURNED_PAYMENT` correction draft with the correction it confirms (a `PAYMENT_RETURN` draft still takes none); (5) the `PAYMENT_RETURN` draft's refusal of a relied-on Payment keeps its message ("return it through a correction of that Final Settlement") also when two Settlements relied on it; the correction then refuses with the known-limit message.

- **V1-056 sub-slice 10c-2b-5, pay back returned Pet Refund-review money after a pet noncompliance termination (BR-DEP-022, BR-SETTLE-008, BR-SETTLE-013, DL-032, DL-053; migration `20261123_119`; owner answer pay back to Q-2026-10-09-61, (a) to Q-2026-10-10-73, (A) and (b) to Q-2026-10-10-75, (a) to Q-2026-10-10-76, (a) to Q-2026-10-11-84; record ops/reviews/V1-056-slice-10c-2b-5-pet-deposit-payback.md):** the money of a Pet Refund-review Refund that comes back to the Pet Deposit is the Customer's, whenever the return was verified; its amount is a running count (a verified return adds, a return reversal and every later Pet Refund-review Refund take out first, never below 0), and the pay-back value is the smaller of that count and what the Pet Deposit holds (0 for a Security Deposit). A Deposit with a forfeiture ground whose held money is above 0 and all pay-back money follows DL-032, also while its forfeiture stays active, so before closure the Final Settlement and after closure every correction that runs the shared DL-032 step applies it to open debt first and refunds the rest (BR-SETTLE-008); the Settlement preview shows `payback_usd_cents`. Approved tightening (Q-73 (a)): a Lease Deposit forfeiture takes only the held money beyond the pay-back value and is refused (22023, "The Deposit holds nothing to forfeit") when nothing is beyond it. Relaxing exception: the returned-Refund correction with a new Refund, which checks the path before the return, also accepts a Pet Deposit whose held money after the return would be all pay-back money. Choices: (1) a Settlement or correction Refund paid from pay-back money and its later return change only what the Deposit holds, not the count, so in a kept Pet Deposit every cent held stays pay-back money; (2) the disposition insert check still accepts any amount up to the held value, because the one-call Lease disposition is owner-only since slice 6 and the forfeiture draft reads the source (slice 12 item: the same limit in the insert check, a further tightening for the owner); (3) the count orders events by time, a return before a Refund at the same instant. Known consequence: a second active forfeiture of a Deposit (the sub-slice 10d guard) is no longer reachable through a forfeiture draft, because money that comes back after a forfeiture is pay-back money; the 10d guard stays and is tested on a hand-built state.

In one transaction, each record linked before it is written, it undoes the uses of the returned Refund's own source (its Credit, or its Deposit) by that correction and by every `HELD_VALUE_REFUND` naming it (their Credit and Deposit applications from that source reversed, newest first, so the debt comes back and stays with its Customers), recovers each of their Refunds from that source by a charge of the exact net amount to the person who received it (the 10e-1c writer), then reverses the return (a linked `CORRECTION_REVERSAL` row). Implementer's reading of "paid from the returned value": only records paid from the returned Refund's own Credit or Deposit are undone; what those corrections paid from the Customer's other Credits or from other Deposits was real money paid to real debt and stays. Refused (55000): a return already reversed; a Refund to recover that has its own return (reverse that later return first); a returned value another path used (undo that use first); uses to undo that are more than the returned amount (a `REFUND_RETURN` with a new Refund also paid out money its source already held, found by review round 1), until the owner answers Q-2026-10-12-95 (recommendation: charge back only what the mistaken return brought back); a Refund to recover paid to someone other than the Deposit's own Customer, until the owner answers Q-2026-10-12-94 (the plan's older text says the Deposit owner pays; the Q-78 rule says the person who received the money; recommendation: the person who received it). No DL-032 step. The general Refund correction check's reversal branch now reads a Deposit Refund's source by `source_deposit_id` (the 10c-2b-2a note), so an over-reversal of any Deposit Refund is refused; before this sub-slice only the Pet Refund-review Refund could reach that branch, so no committed result changes. - **V1-056 sub-slice 10e-3c, only the mistaken amount comes back when returned money also paid debt (BR-SETTLE-013, BR-SETTLE-016, DL-032; DB-SETTLE-005; owner answer (a) to Q-2026-10-12-96; migration `20261202_128`):** a `RETURN_REVERSAL` whose uses are more than the returned amount while its Refunds paid out less than it is no longer refused. Each Refund is charged back whole; the newest Credit or Deposit applications of the uses are reversed whole until the rest of the returned amount (that amount less the Refunds' nets) is reached; the part of the last of them that was not returned money is applied again, in the same correction, to the same obligation from the same Credit or Deposit, right after the return is reversed and linked before it is written. In the owner's example ($300 returned only, then $1,700 with a new Refund; the $2,000 Credit pays a $1,500 charge and refunds $500) the $500 Refund is charged back, the $1,500 application is reversed and $300 applied again: the Customer owes $500 and $1,200 of the charge, exactly the mistaken $1,700 (the test runs it at 1/100 scale, 300 cents for $300; the rule does not depend on scale). The source names the part (`reapply`, at most one entry, empty in every other case); the recorder stores a one-step `plan` from it, which the Settlement Credit writer reads and the Deposit application check matches (internal `app.settlement_return_reversal_reapply_steps`, no grant); a Deposit part keeps the reversed application's stage and target and is numbered after the Settlement's highest application number (the design said "order"; implementer's reading). The design's fallback writer for a Credit part was not needed: the existing writer's basis rules accept the restoration (tested on charge lines). Fail closed (review round 1): the part must be a listed application of the returned Refund's own Credit or Deposit, with the same Credit or Deposit, the same obligation kind and, for a Late-payment Charge or a Deposit's line, the same target, only in that case, above 0 and below the application; the reversal brings back exactly the returned amount when the uses are more than it, never more; the confirm accepts only the plan built from its source and a payload with exactly the recorder's keys. The result and audit event name the part (`reapplied`). Known limits (the confirm refuses, no money moves): a Credit part on a Rent or Service Invoice without designation is refused (23514) if the Rent-first proposal no longer gives its line; a Deposit part is refused when the Deposit's path is no longer DL-032 or the first Pet Deposit stage's line is no longer pet damage; a Credit part is refused when the Credit's Payment is no longer received; the Deposit writer dates the part by the clock only, so a reversal row dated ahead of the clock could make it refused (not seen). A `RETURN_REVERSAL` draft recorded before revision 128 is stale (P5S02) and keeps a new draft of the same correction waiting: staff reject it and record it again. Lock order (security review note): the lock function does not lock the re-applied target's Invoice lines in its passes; the Credit writer locks them after the Invoice row, as every other writer does, so no new lock cycle. For sub-slice 10e-3d (independent review note): the re-applied application uses money an earlier return-only correction brought back but is linked to the reversal correction, so 10e-3d must count it against that earlier correction's left value.

- **V1-056 sub-slice 10e-3d-1, every correction's use of returned money counts (BR-SETTLE-008, BR-SETTLE-013, BR-SETTLE-016, BR-CREDIT-014, DL-032; DB-SETTLE-005; owner answer (a) to Q-2026-10-12-97 and its detail of 2026-10-13; migration `20261203_129`):** 10e-3d is split (owner allowed): 10e-3d-1 builds the count and the reversal limit; 10e-3d-2 (how a reversal charges money another correction paid out, and other Settlements' corrections) waits for Q-2026-10-13-100, because it changes who pays. A new internal count walks the Settlement's corrections oldest first, each with what it did at its own time; what a correction drew from a Credit or Deposit (applications, Refunds and reversed returns, and for a Deposit its receipt reversals and forfeitures, less the applications it reversed, the Refunds it recovered by a charge and, for a Deposit, its own receipts and forfeiture reversals, so it pays out the money it released first; a correction that reverses the Credit draws all the Credit still holds; the receipt, forfeiture and Credit reversal terms since review round 2) takes first from its own return into it, then from the earlier correction it names (a `HELD_VALUE_REFUND` or a `RETURN_REVERSAL`), then from the other returns, oldest first. The left values (`app.settlement_held_deposit_value`, `app.settlement_held_credit_value`) are that count's, so a sweep by a correction that does not name the earlier correction now lowers them; in the Q-97 case X1's $1,000 is used by X2's Refund, X1 has nothing left, and a held-value Refund naming X1 is refused also after X3 brings money back. Implementer's reading (not a free choice): a correction's own return is taken first, because the committed 10e-3b and 10e-3c reversal of a correction with a new Refund charges back exactly its own returned amount; taking the older return first would count the same money twice. A reversal of an earlier return takes only its own left value: a positive part of its money that another correction paid out (`swept_usd_cents`) is refused (55000, "Another correction paid out this return's money; reversing it waits for the owner") until sub-slice 10e-3d-2 builds the owner's answer (a) to Q-100; a missing part is refused as an incomplete source. Since review round 2 the source also names the earlier correction's `left_usd_cents`, and a reversal that would take more than it from the source is refused ("The returned value is no longer available; undo its other use first"), for example when a Refund of the uses came back through a later return. Before 10e-3d-1 such a reversal was refused only when the source held too little, and otherwise took money a later return brought back. Only uses made by the Settlement's corrections count; ordinary Credit spending stays the Q-2026-10-09-63 known limit. The `HELD_VALUE_REFUND` Credit cap still leaves out the confirming correction's own records (the `except` argument; committed tests unchanged). A `HELD_VALUE_REFUND` or `RETURN_REVERSAL` draft recorded before revision 129 whose source now reads differently is stale (P5S02).

- **V1-056 sub-slice 10e-3d-1 review round 1 (independent and security; record ops/reviews/V1-056-slice-10e-3d-1-returned-value-count.md):** independent: one blocker, fixed: the first count read each correction's records as they are now (applications not reversed, Refunds less every recovery), so a `REFUND` correction that releases an application (reversed whole, its rest written again) and refunds the released part was counted as using the returned money, although it paid out only the money it released (and a later reversal of a counted application made the earlier correction's use smaller while its release stayed). The count now takes each correction's net draw at its own time: what it paid out (applications, Refunds, reversed returns) less what it brought back (its reversals of applications from the source and its recoveries by a charge), never below 0; a `RETURN_REVERSAL` names its earlier correction, so its return reversal empties that entry. Tested on the real path (an ordinary application of 1,500, then a `REFUND` correction of 500: the return keeps 1,800 left and nothing swept). Two should-fix: the order rules are now proven by a test (three returns of 300, 400 and 200; a held-value Refund naming the 200 one pays 500 of debt and refunds 200: the named 200 first, then the oldest 300, then 200 of the 400); "The Deposit holds no returned money to refund" lost its only tests, because the counted paths can no longer reach it (a counted sweep now empties the left value first): it stays as a backstop for the known limits (records the count leaves out, such as a Deposit receipt reversal by a 10e-1b or 10e-2 correction), and its Credit sibling "The Credit holds no returned value to refund" is tested after ordinary spending.
