- **V1-056 sub-slice 10e-3d-2a, a return's reversal undoes the money another correction paid out (BR-SETTLE-008, BR-SETTLE-013, BR-SETTLE-016, BR-CREDIT-014, BR-REFUND-015, DL-032; DB-SETTLE-005, DB-REFUND-002; owner answer (a) to Q-2026-10-13-100 point 1; migration `20261204_130`):** the 10e-3d-1 count becomes one internal walk that the count (same results) and a new internal takes function both read. For an earlier return-only correction E, the takes are the records of each other correction S (neither E nor one naming E) that paid out part of E's money: inside S the money S brought back pays out first, then S's Refunds from the source, the oldest first, then S's applications, the newest first (the owner answers to Q-2026-10-10-76 and Q-2026-10-12-95: a new Refund pays the returned money first). E's reversal now undoes those parts too: a Refund part is charged back to the person who received that Refund (a share, the 10e-1c charge: this Lease when that person is its signed Customer, else no Lease), an application part reverses the application whole and applies the rest again to the same obligation from the same Credit or Deposit, linked (as 10e-3c, now one part per such application). Together with the own uses they undo exactly E's used money, so the reversal takes only E's left value. In the owner's example as tested (Pet Deposit, scaled to the fixture): X1 brings back 2,000; X2 brings back 500, the Customer's Credit pays 300 of a 1,500 charge, the Pet Deposit 1,200, and 1,300 is refunded; X1's reversal charges 800 to the Refund's recipient and makes 1,200 of the charge owed again. Implementer's readings (fail closed): an S that also paid out through a reversal of the Credit, a reversed return, a Deposit receipt reversal or a forfeiture is not split, and its part is refused with its own message (10e-3d-2c, or the forfeiture refusal of owner answer (a) to Q-2026-10-13-103 point 2); an application reversed since waits for 10e-3d-2b; a Refund part more than the Refund's net is refused ("undo its other use first"). The own uses are undone against the part of E's money they used (E's used less its swept part). The source's parts must add up and be listed exactly, else it is incomplete. A `RETURN_REVERSAL` draft recorded before revision 130 is stale (P5S02).

No assertion changed; the refusals of a signing time one day ahead and one microsecond before the last signature are now measured from the database's clock. The app's signature check is unchanged. Review round 1 hardening (fail closed): a part not inside its payment stops open, and while following a reversed return's stretches only changes by strictly earlier corrections are followed, so the recursion ends with a clean refusal.

- **V1-056 signing time from the database clock (owner answer (a) to Q-2026-10-14-110; BR-AUDIT-003, API-036, API-038, UI-038, UI-040; no migration; record ops/reviews/V1-056-signing-time-database-clock.md):** a Signer's signature time and the Lease signing time are the database's own time at the command. The two signing request bodies (`PATCH /lease-signers/{signer_id}`, `POST /leases/{lease_id}/sign`) are `event_id` and `reason` only; a body that still sends `signed_at` is refused with 422 (the models keep `extra="forbid"`). The routes pass no time; the service passes `COALESCE(%s::timestamptz, statement_timestamp())` to `app.record_lease_signature` and `app.sign_lease_with_reservation`, the same statement time the unchanged database checks compare with, so a device clock can neither refuse a signing nor make one look earlier. A retry with the same Idempotency-Key replays the first result (the database replays before it reads the time). The staff screen sends no `new Date()` time for either action. Implementer's reading (both round 1 reviewers found it acceptable): the service commands keep an optional explicit time, which no route passes, so the committed database tests keep checking the database refusals they check today (a Signer signature time later than the statement time; a Lease signing time earlier than a Signer's signature or later than the statement time) through the service; the unchanged "not before the Signer was added" check has no committed test. Docs: docs/002 BR-AUDIT-003, docs/005 API-036 and API-038, docs/006 UI-040. New Q-2026-10-14-112 (other times the screens take from the device clock, for example the termination `occurred_at`; the database-level limit that the server's own role can still pass an earlier time; nothing waits).

- **V1-056 sub-slice 10e-3d-2c, money of a return that left through a bounced Payment or a wrong receipt (BR-SETTLE-013, BR-SETTLE-016, BR-REFUND-015, BR-CREDIT-014, DL-032; DB-SETTLE-005, DB-REFUND-002; owner answer (a) to Q-2026-10-13-103 point 1; migration `20261210_136`; record ops/reviews/V1-056-slice-10e-3d-2c-return-reversal-returned-refund.md):** a `RETURNED_PAYMENT` or `DEPOSIT_RECEIPT_CORRECTION` correction C recovers the Refunds paid from the money it takes back, reverses the payments made from it and then the source, while it charges an earlier return E's returned Refund R's recipient only R's net, which E had lowered. E's `RETURN_REVERSAL` now charges every part of E's money that left with C's reversal of the source (C's own take; a stretch on a payment C reversed; a Refund part above its net that C's recovery covers) to the person who received R, in one charge-back of R, and nothing else; a part that cannot be followed stays open and is refused with the reworded message "A Credit reversal or a Deposit receipt reversal paid out this return's money in a way this reversal cannot follow yet; reversing it waits for the owner". Implementer's design changes, confirmed by the round 1 independent reviewer under the run rule of 2026-10-14 (none changes who pays or how much): (1) the general Refund correction check counts R's listed charge-back as available for the reversal of E's return (after C the source holds nothing and a Credit's Payment is reversed); (2) R's charge-back takes the reversal's exact time, written right after it, because the deferred Credit and Deposit history checks group events by time and R's net cannot go below 0 first (targeted run T1 failed on both history checks before this); (3) the design's refusal of an R with another active return is not built: the committed test the design names as allowed has one (the later correction's real 500 return), and C charged only the net every return had lowered, so each reversal charges back only its own money, capped by R's net after the reversal; (4) an own use's Refund that such a C charged back sends the source down the walk path, so it is charged back the same way (before: refused as no longer available); (5) the follow function hands such a stretch back with no record id and the source names R. R's charge-back row is dated a few microseconds before the charge Invoice it names (nothing reads that order). Known text item: the charge reads "Recovery of Refund N paid from value whose return was recorded by mistake" (the writer's fixed sentence; wording for slice 11e or the owner).

A `RETURN_REVERSAL` R whose earlier return's money a correction of another closed Final Settlement B paid out through a Credit application reverses that application whole and puts back the rest on its own line, every record on B linked to a companion correction of B: a `SETTLEMENT_CORRECTION` draft of B, variant `RETURN_REVERSAL_COMPANION`, id derived from R's draft and B, written in R's confirm under `final_settlements.prepare` with R's reason, prepared and confirmed by R's approver (implementer's reading of "recorded and confirmed by the same approver"; nothing in it is chosen by the approver: it is B's slice of R's confirmed source), never pending; R and the companion name each other (R's source, result and audit event; the companion's payload and its own audit event on B's Lease). B's own rules pass unchanged. The walk treats a companion as part of its reversal. Lock order: the Settlement draft locks of R's and every companion's Settlement in id order, then their invoice-lease locks and Lease rows in Lease id order, before the lock function. Still refused: a take whose correction also refunded from the Credit (`OTHER_SETTLEMENT`, 2d-2b), another Settlement's Credit reversal or return reversal, and B's own Final Settlement confirm's use (2d-2c). Known limit (fail closed): a payment that a correction of another Settlement, a companion included, changed stops the follow function, so a later reversal of another return whose money sat in it is refused. Implementer's changes to the written design, confirmed by the reviewers of round 2 under the run rule of 2026-10-14 (none changes who pays or how much): (1) the source's `companions` entries carry no derived ids (the confirm derives them from its draft, so nothing in the payload names the companion); (2) the placed function does not merge companions (a reversal taker is always opened by its return reversal record; the merge with an OR join timed out deep follow chains in P1); (3) a new internal `app.settlement_credit_application_owner` decides which Settlement a listed Credit application belongs to (its own, else the Final Settlement of its target's Lease; review round 1 blocker: the rest a `REFUND` correction writes again has none); (4) the successor and follow functions rank only R's own Settlement's `reapply` entries against R's linked put-backs (review round 1); (5) R's and the companions' records are dated after every companion header (review round 1); (6) the companion's audit events are written after `SET CONSTRAINTS ALL IMMEDIATE`.

- **V1-056 sub-slice 10e-3d-2d-2b-1, a take by another Lease's correction that also paid a Refund from the returned Credit is undone through the companion (BR-SETTLE-013, BR-SETTLE-016, BR-CREDIT-014; DB-SETTLE-005; owner answers (a) to Q-2026-10-13-100 point 2 and Q-2026-10-13-103 point 3; migration `20261213_139`; record ops/reviews/V1-056-slice-10e-3d-2d-2b-1-other-refunding-take.md):** 10e-3d-2d-2b split (owner allowed): 2b-1 (this), 2b-2 (the companion charge-back of a Refund part of another Settlement's correction and another Settlement's bounced Payment take; built when a real path is shown, else asked first). Pre-code finding (plan, "10e-3d-2d-2b pre-code note"), corrected in review round 1: a correction's draw covers, in order, what it brought back itself (the draw's offset), its own return, then the return it names, before any other return's money, and its records are laid out Refunds first, then applications, the newest first; every Credit Refund writer caps its Refund by one of those three (a `REFUND` correction by what it released, a `REFUND_RETURN` by its own return, a held-value Refund by its named return's left value) or pays it from a Credit it creates itself, so a return's money taken by another Lease's correction lands on its applications (the 10e-3d-2a round 2 reviewer confirmed the same for one Settlement; the 2b-1 round 1 independent reviewer found no real path through a take). The placed function therefore no longer makes the whole take of such a correction one open `OTHER_SETTLEMENT` part because it also paid a Refund; a part that falls on any record of that correction other than a Credit application (an allow-list, security review round 1) stays one open `OTHER_SETTLEMENT` part named by that correction, refused with its existing message. A take by another Settlement's correction that also reversed the Credit or a return is still refused, now with the `CREDIT_REVERSAL` message or the general one. Review round 1 found the real path to another Settlement's Refund: through the follow function, when another Settlement's `REFUND` correction changed the payment holding the return's money (today refused as `CHANGED_APPLICATION`, set-up R1 in the review record); that is 2b-2. It also found that another Settlement's bounced Payment cannot take the return's money (the returned Credit is relied on by the first Settlement, so the other Settlement's `RETURNED_PAYMENT` is refused). Exact-text patches of the placed function only.

- **V1-056 sub-slice 10e-3d-2d-2b-2, a return's money on a payment that another Lease's `REFUND` correction changed is followed into its Refund and payments and undone through the companion (BR-SETTLE-013, BR-SETTLE-016, BR-CREDIT-014; DB-SETTLE-005, DB-REFUND-002; owner answers (a) to Q-2026-10-13-103 point 3 and Q-2026-10-13-107, owner answer 4 of 2026-10-16; migration `20261214_140`; pre-code note in the plan; set-up R1 of the 2b-1 review record):** the follow function reads a changing correction of another Final Settlement when the source is a Credit and its variant is `REFUND` (an allow-list; every other correction of another Settlement still stops as `CHANGED_APPLICATION`) and follows the stretch into its Refunds, the oldest first, and payments, the newest first, as for a `REFUND` correction of the reversal's own Settlement (owner answer (a) to Q-107). A part on its Refund is charged back to the recipient on that Settlement's Lease when the recipient is its signed Customer, else on no Lease (owner answer 4); a part on its payment is reversed as in 2d-2a; both go through the companion correction of that Settlement, which links the charge-back, its charge and its Invoice (the closed Settlement's guards require that link) and names them in its result entry and audit event. New internal `app.settlement_refund_owner` (no grant). The recovery check allows a charge-back linked to a companion confirmed by the same approver in the same transaction when its return reversal, confirmed there too, lists the Refund; a row linked to the reversal alone stays refused twice over (the Refund's closed Final Settlement must link it, and the recovery check's own `RETURN_REVERSAL` branch takes only a Refund of no other Final Settlement, security review round 2; no test can isolate either layer, because a row is linked to one correction only). The share check reads the companion's draft too (implementer's addition found at build: without it a charge-back of a part of the Refund's net would be refused; it reads only a draft confirmed in the same transaction). The refusal function also checks the companions against the Refund parts and that such a charge-back names that Settlement or no Lease; the `OTHER_SETTLEMENT` message is reworded ("... in a way this reversal cannot undo; reversing it waits for the owner"; it now stands only for a part on another Settlement's Refund reached through a take, for which no real path was found). Not built: another Settlement's bounced Payment take (no real path; its refusal stays). A charge on no Lease for another Settlement's Refund is defensive: its recipient is always a signed Customer of that Lease (a `REFUND` correction's line is on its Lease, a Credit Refund goes to the Credit's own Customer, a Credit application's target Customer is the Credit's, and an Invoice on a Lease goes only to a signed Customer; independent review round 1 found no real path), so it has no real-path test (a limit). Every companion's draft source, result entry and audit event now carry `recoveries`, `[]` when there is none (additive; no reader compares exact keys). 10e-3d-2d-2c moves to migration `20261215_141`.

- **V1-056 sub-slice 10e-3d-2d-2c, another Lease's own Final Settlement confirm that used a returned Credit counts against the return and is undone through the companion (BR-SETTLE-013, BR-SETTLE-016, BR-CREDIT-014, DL-032; DB-SETTLE-005; owner answer (a) to Q-2026-10-15-113; migration `20261215_141`; pre-code note in the plan; record ops/reviews/V1-056-slice-10e-3d-2d-2c-settlement-confirm.md):** a Final Settlement's own confirm writes its Credit applications with the Settlement and no correction link, so the walk did not see them. For a Credit, the walk now takes each Final Settlement whose own confirm applied it as a walker, at the time of its first such application, in the one order by time and id with the corrections (its id in the walk is the Final Settlement's); it draws the sum of those applications and takes the returns' money, the oldest first. It is a walker only while some return's money is left at its place in the order, so a confirm before every return into that Credit (as in every committed set-up) gives no row and no committed result changes. The placed function places such a take on the confirm's applications from the Credit, the newest first, and a source part then carries the Final Settlement's id in `settlement_correction_id`; the follow function takes an application with no correction link and a `final_settlement_id` as written by that Final Settlement (before, it stopped open). The return's reversal lists such an application for undoing, names its Settlement as a companion, reverses it whole linked to the companion and puts back any rest through the companion's step (sub-slice 10e-3d-2d-2a, unchanged); a later reversal of another return whose money sits in that put-back stops as `CHANGED_APPLICATION` (the 2d-2a limit). This narrows the known limit of owner answer 2 to Q-2026-10-09-63 for this case only. No design change; no new function, grant, table or lock. Not built: a confirm's Deposit applications (a Deposit belongs to one Lease, and its confirm comes before every correction of that Lease).

- **V1-056 sub-slice 10f-1, the mistaken credit Adjustment reversal before closure (BR-INV-044, BR-CREDIT-006, BR-CREDIT-008, BR-AUTH-010, BR-SETTLE-013; DB-INV-010, DB-CREDIT-002; owner answer 7 to Q-2026-10-06-36 and the slice 10 entry of the plan, from the owner answer to the 8f report; migration `20261219_145`, relaxing changes and new functions; pre-code design in the plan; record ops/reviews/V1-056-slice-10f-1-adjustment-reversal-draft.md):** 10f is split (allowed without asking): 10f-1 the ordinary draft before closure, 10f-2 the `ADJUSTMENT_REVERSAL` correction after closure. An `invoices.adjust` holder records a draft of the new kind `ADJUSTMENT_REVERSAL` (`app.record_adjustment_reversal_draft`) naming a credit Adjustment recorded by mistake; a `financial.approve` holder confirms it (`app.confirm_adjustment_reversal`). The confirm writes the first `app.invoice_adjustment_reversals` row (the draft's reason, the approver, `financial.approve`), restores the line's obligation, and for each paid value the Adjustment released (migration 67) applies the part of its Credit still available back to the Adjustment's line, never more than the release and the line's unpaid rest, earlier put-backs from the same Credit counted; the rest of the release stays as debt on the line. Each put-back is a Credit application of the Invoice Customer's own Credit with the Rent-first proposal for its amount (`credits.apply`, the approver as actor, a detail trace naming the reversal and the release). One `invoice.adjustment_reversed` audit event. The draft kind, preparer, kind-preparer and WITHDRAWN checks gain `ADJUSTMENT_REVERSAL` and `invoices.adjust`; the two capability-scoped draft reads accept nine capabilities. Refused (55000): a debit Adjustment, a reversed one, one on an Invoice that is not issued or is VOID, one that a hand-back or unpaid-Initial resolution wrote (Q-2026-10-16-118 point 2), one linked to a post-settlement correction, one whose Lease's Final Settlement is closed (10f-2), a second waiting draft, and, until the owner answers Q-2026-10-16-118 point 1, a put-back that the proposal order (Rent, Service Charges, then other lines by line order) would put on another line, on any Invoice. A pending `ADJUSTMENT_REVERSAL` draft does not block a Final Settlement; after the closure it is stale. A released Credit application's Credit is fungible: its available value may include Credit the Customer held before the Adjustment, and the put-back still never exceeds the release. No table, column, trigger or other grant change. Service: new module `property_rental/adjustment_reversal.py`; routes and screens in slice 11.

A restoration of a recovery charge (a DEBIT Adjustment of its line, the reversal of a credit Adjustment of its line by the 10f-1 draft or the 10f-2 correction, or the same charge billed again and issued after a VOID, that is an issue when another Invoice of the same obligation exists) is refused (55000, "A forfeiture recorded while this recovery charge was forgiven is still active; reverse the forfeiture first") while a forfeiture of the recovered Refund's Pet Deposit that relied on the lower count is not reversed. Implementer's reading for the reviewers: a forfeiture relied on the lower count when it was recorded at or after the charge's first issue at a time when the charge stood lower than it stands after the restoration (its insert check read a count lowered by this charge's forgiveness; option (a)'s "recorded after the forgiveness"); a forfeiture recorded before the forgiveness never blocks, and a forgiveness stays open. - **V1-056 sub-slice 10e-2b-4e-1, a returned Payment of a shared Deposit charges back only the shortfall (BR-SETTLE-013, BR-SETTLE-016, BR-REFUND-015, DL-032, DL-053; DB-REFUND-002, DB-DEP-002, DB-DEP-007, DB-PAY-009; owner answer (a) to Q-2026-10-18-127; migration `20261231_157`, four new internal functions and exact-text patches; pre-code design in the plan, the 10e-2b-4e entry; record ops/reviews/V1-056-slice-10e-2b-4e-1-shared-deposit-shortfall.md):** 10e-2b-4e is split: 4e-1 builds the return before closure (the `PAYMENT_RETURN` draft); 4e-2 builds the `RETURNED_PAYMENT` correction and the receipt correction after closure, after the owner's answer to Q-2026-10-18-134 point 1. For a Deposit the returned Payment funded that also holds another Payment's active receipt (a shared Deposit), the shortfall is the returned Payment's receipt less what the Deposit holds, never below 0: a shortfall of 0 charges nothing and the receipt is reversed while the Refund stays out (paid from the other Payments' money); a shortfall above 0 is charged back to the recipient of the Deposit's Refunds that are not fully returned, newest first, each at most its net, and the Deposit ends at 0. A Deposit the returned Payment alone funded is unchanged (its shortfall is the nets of its Refunds). A shared Deposit whose unreturned Refunds went to more than one person keeps the shared refusal while its shortfall is above 0 (Q-2026-10-18-134 point 2). The recovery insert check accepts a share only inside a confirmed `PAYMENT_RETURN` of this transaction, at most the Deposit's shortfall before the row; a smaller sum is refused by the held-history check; the receipt reversal check lets that return reverse its Payment's receipt of a shared Deposit whose Refund stays out. Option (d) stays until 4e-2 (review round 2, below). Design change during the build (targeted run T2): the design patched `app.payment_return_source`, but the `RETURNED_PAYMENT` correction's source extends that function, so the change reached the correction (a committed after-closure test got another refusal message); the recorder and the confirm of the `PAYMENT_RETURN` draft now read a new `app.payment_return_draft_source` instead, and `app.payment_return_source` is unchanged (confirmed needed and safe by the round 1 independent reviewer). Review round 1 (independent and security; no blocker), fixed: the planned check no longer compares a shared Deposit's shortfall while it has an active forfeiture or application, so the forfeiture and application refusals keep their message (independent should-fix 1); the option (d) refusal stays for a Deposit whose unreturned Refunds went to more than one person (55000, "The Deposit's Refunds that are not fully returned went to more than one person; this receipt is not recorded here"), because that Deposit's return stays refused (independent should-fix 2; Q-2026-10-18-134 point 2); a shared Deposit with a Reservation outcome Refund or a charge on a closed Settlement's Lease keeps those refusals also with a shortfall of 0 (both reviewers' note); new tests: a shortfall that reaches an older Refund, the two-recipient refusals and the two-recipient case with a shortfall of 0, a receipt between the record and the confirm (P5S02), the forfeiture refusal order, the shortfall-share check with and without a Settlement. Known limit kept: the rule reads only what the Deposit holds, not the order of events (security note); after closure a shared Deposit's return stays refused until 4e-2. Review round 2 (independent and security; no blocker), fixed under the round-3 rule: option (d) is kept unchanged until 4e-2 (both reviewers: a narrowed (d) did not close the deliberate path for two recipients, and without (d) a receipt recorded while a Refund is out could reach the refused correction after closure; the owner said "(d) until (a) is built", and (a) includes the corrections), so the receipt writer is not patched, the round 1 two-recipient receipt refusal is dropped with it, and the committed 4d tests of option (d) keep their HEAD form; the round 1 test of a receipt between the record and the confirm becomes a verified partial return between them; known limits named in Q-2026-10-18-134 point 2 (a shared Deposit reaches unreturned Refunds to two people by a receipt before the Refunds, a pending Refund draft confirmed after a receipt, or a reversed verified return; its return stays refused until point 2 is answered); the plan's Q-127 known-limit line updated. Review round 3: security clean; independent two text should-fix (stale wording of the dropped receipt-writer change, the record's log line, the slice 12 items), fixed under the round-3 text rule with no round 4; the review notes for slice 12 are in the plan's slice 12 list.

The correction moves only the wrong allocation, which is still active, so its value never became Credit or a Refund; the Payment's Credit and Refunds and the Settlement's use of them do not change, and who pays and how much change exactly as in 10g. The move source has one body, the new internal `app.wrong_unit_move_source(property, allocation, target invoice, settlement correction)` (no grant), built in the migration from the current slice 7 body by two exact-text replacements (its name and fourth argument; the refusal keeps the blanket condition and, for a correction, also needs the release); `app.payment_move_source` keeps its signature and settings and calls it with false, so the slice 7 move draft keeps the blanket rule and its refusals in their order; `app.settlement_payment_move_source` calls it with true. What it relied on is the definition of sub-slice 10e-1a: a record on an obligation of its Lease (an Invoice of the Lease, or a Late-payment Charge whose source Invoice is of the Lease) made at or before the closure, a Final Settlement Credit application, and a record linked to one of its corrections (a re-posted rest, a put-back, a DL-032 Credit step, the new allocation of a `PAYMENT_MOVE` correction on another Lease). New internal `app.closed_settlements_relying_on_allocation` and `app.closed_settlements_relying_on_credit_application` (no grant) name those Settlements; new BEFORE INSERT triggers `a0_payment_allocation_reversals_relied_on` and `a1_customer_credit_application_reversals_relied_on` (the latter after the 8e-2 and 10c-1b refusals, whose texts stay first) refuse (P5S01, the 8e-1 text "A closed Final Settlement changes only through a post-settlement correction") a reversal not linked by `app.settlement_correction_linked` to a correction of each such Settlement, after the insert check's own locks and the Settlement row FOR SHARE (the 8e-1 order). So the one-call allocation and Credit application reversals are refused (owner answer 3), the ordinary credit Adjustment and another Lease's `REFUND` correction cannot release a 10g target allocation (Q-120 point 2), the post-closure put-back of an `ADJUSTMENT_REVERSAL` correction cannot be undone by the one-call reversal (the owner note's first choice; who pays and how much do not change), the 10c-1a path (a one-call reversal, then a `CHARGE_REDUCTION` of the reopened line) is closed, and a record two closed Settlements relied on stays refused (the known limit of Q-120 point 1). `app.payment_move_source` refuses (55000, "A closed Final Settlement relied on this allocation; move it through a correction of that Final Settlement") such an allocation before the slice 7 body, so the slice 7 recorder and confirm refuse it (owner answer 4 and Q-120 point 2); an allocation reversed at or before the closure is not one the Settlement relied on and keeps the slice 7 rules (review round 1, independent S1). Each trigger takes the insert check's own locks before it reads the Settlement rows, so a Settlement started or closed during a lock wait is seen (review round 1, security note 1). Records made after the closure and not linked stay reversible (owner answer 3). The allocation service maps P5S01 to a conflict (it was "unavailable, replay"); the Credit service gives the closed-Settlement text for the new refusal and keeps its 8e-2 text. Implementer's readings for the reviewers: "existed at closure" is read as the 10e-1a "relied on", so a correction's own records count too; the refusal is at insert, for every writer, because every correction writer already links its reversals before it writes them; the 8e-1 text keeps every committed assertion of a credit Adjustment on a closed Lease, whose release reversal is now refused first with the same code and text.

- **V1-056 sub-slice 10h-1b, the Credit Refund outside a correction (BR-SETTLE-013, BR-SETTLE-004, BR-CREDIT-011, BR-CREDIT-014, BR-REFUND-002, BR-AUTH-010, DL-032; DB-SETTLE-005; owner answers (b) to Q-2026-10-19-141 and (a) to Q-2026-10-19-144; migration `20270109_166`, four new internal functions, one new trigger and three exact-text replacements; pre-code design in the plan, the 10h entry; record ops/reviews/V1-056-slice-10h-1b-returned-credit-refund.md):** money that a post-settlement correction brought back into a Customer Credit (a returned Refund's `VALUE_CORRECTION` linked to a correction) leaves only through a correction of that Final Settlement, the `HELD_VALUE_REFUND` correction naming the return, which pays the Customer's own open debt on the Lease first (DL-032). New internal `app.credit_settlement_returned_value_left` sums what every such return has left by the returned-value count (sub-slices 10e-3d to 10e-3d-2d); new internal `app.refuse_credit_refund_of_returned_value` raises P5S01 when that sum is above 0 and the Refund amount is more than the Credit's available value less it. The ordinary Credit Refund draft recorders (`app.record_refund_draft`, variant `USD` with a `CREDIT` source, and `app.record_credit_customer_refund_draft`) call it after their current-state checks; `app.confirm_refund_draft` calls it for a Credit source after the Credit Refund locks, so the draft stays pending. The Refund service maps P5S01 of a draft command to a conflict (409; it read as "unavailable, replay"). Implementer's reading for the reviewers: the refusal compares the amount with the Credit's money other than the returned money (available less left), so money the Credit holds for other reasons stays refundable (the owner's option (b)), and a left value above what the Credit holds refuses every ordinary Refund of that Credit (fail closed). A Refund draft waiting on the Credit already blocks the return-only correction's record, so the confirm's refusal is a backstop. Review round 1: each Settlement's walk also lists other Settlements' entries for the Credit, so the sum counts only each Settlement's own corrections' entries (independent S1); the security reviewer found that the one-call Credit reversal can still move that money back to its Payment; review round 2 (security) showed that for a Payment confirmed for a named Invoice or Late-payment Charge the Payment Refund's eligibility check reads only that target, so the money could leave in cash while the Customer owes on the closed Lease (Q-2026-10-19-144). Owner answer (a) to Q-2026-10-19-144, built in the same migration: a new BEFORE INSERT trigger on `app.customer_credit_reversals` (internal `app.refuse_returned_credit_reversal`, no grant) takes the Credit Refund locks first and refuses (P5S01, the 8e-1 text, which the Credit service already maps to a conflict) a Credit reversal while a return into the Credit has money left, unless a correction of each such Settlement confirmed in the same transaction links it; the `RETURNED_PAYMENT` correction links first and still reverses the Credit; the per-Settlement count is the new internal `app.credit_settlement_returned_value_by_settlement`, which the sum now reads. Only a returned Refund recorded by a correction counts as money brought back; other value a correction puts back into a Credit (for example a correction's reversal of a Credit application) is not counted (review round 2, security S1). Ordinary Credit applications outside a correction stay as the known limit of owner answer 2 to Q-2026-10-09-63; the Payment and Pet Deposit Refund drafts, the correction writers and the owner-only one-call `app.create_usd_refund` are not changed.

Review round 1: a termination stamped with the database's time is refused (40001, "record it again") when a Deposit balance event or required-amount adjustment of the Lease is dated after its time, because it was saved while the termination waited and the ground would not read it; a required-amount adjustment is dated with `clock_timestamp()` after its Deposit lock; the Pet departure writer locks the Lease before its Pet Deposit, so it never deadlocks with a termination. ## DL-070 — Lease agreement wording: serious-breach termination and the Article 2.5 clause reference

- **Type:** `OWNER BUSINESS DECISION`
- **Status:** `APPROVED; NOT IMPLEMENTED`
- **Source:** the owner, with the new standard Lease agreement wording of 2026-10-15; recorded on 2026-10-20 in docs-only rules update 1 (ops/V1_056_TAKEOVER.md section 8). V1-056 stays paused before slice 11.
- **Amends:** DL-016 with BR-LEASE-024 and PR-LEASE-024 (serious-breach exception); DL-064 with BR-LEASE-025 and PR-LEASE-025 (clause reference). The decision text of DL-016 and DL-064 is unchanged; each has one linking line.
- **DL-016 before this entry:** at least three documented warning letters are required before a Lease is terminated for a Customer violation; the violation and the termination authority must come from the signed Lease; the system must not invent violations, penalties, fees, forfeitures or termination rights.
- **Serious-breach exception:** a serious breach by the Customer, meaning a crime or danger to people or the building, may end the Lease at once, without the three warning letters. The authority still comes from the signed Lease: the new standard Lease agreement contains this clause (BR-LEASE-025). The termination is still a separate explicit action by an authorized user, with its grounds, evidence reference and clause reference recorded; nothing is automatic. Every other Customer violation still needs the three warning letters. The exception fits as BR-LEASE-025 already treats the unpaid-Initial ground: a signed-Lease ground to which BR-LEASE-024's three warning letters do not apply.
- **Clause reference for the unpaid-Initial ground (DL-064, BR-LEASE-005, BR-LEASE-025):** the signed-Lease clause that gives the termination right when the Security Deposit or the Initial Rent Invoice is not fully paid within five calendar days after the Lease Start Date is Article 2.5 of the standard Lease agreement. A termination on that ground records "Article 2.5" as its clause reference.
- **Open (asked in the 2026-10-20 report; nothing is built before the answer):** the deposit outcome of a serious-breach termination. It is not decided by this entry; as a violation termination, DL-069 would keep the Security Deposit and let the Pet Deposit pay pet damage first (both kept for pet noncompliance).
- **Today's system (not changed by this entry):** a `CUSTOMER_VIOLATION` termination is refused with fewer than three warnings (`lease_termination.py`), and the signed-Lease clause reference is staff-entered text. The exception and any "Article 2.5" default are built in a later slice, only when the owner sends it.
- **Not recorded by this entry:** the other points of the new Lease agreement (landlord 30 days' notice; the day-20 warning, day-30 default notice and termination notice as the three nonpayment letters; no automatic renewal and renewal intent 30 days before the End Date; Security Deposit refund within 7 days after the final inspection and the final Utility Invoice; no Rent for the month when the Unit is handed back on the 4th at the latest). They were checked against the current docs and their differences reported to the owner; the current rules stay.
- **Answered by DL-073 (owner, 2026-10-20 and 2026-10-21):** the open item above is closed: a serious-breach termination keeps the Security Deposit like any violation termination, and the Pet Deposit pays pet damage first with the rest refunded (both kept for a pet-rule breach). DL-073 also records the other Lease points listed above, and that Article 15.5 (no Rent when the Apartment is handed back before the 5th) is removed from the Lease files dated 2026-10-20; Article 2.5 stays the clause reference of the unpaid-Initial ground.
- **Decision date:** 2026-10-15.

## DL-071 — Deployment readiness, data rules and the release gate (V1-059, V1-060)

- **Type:** `OWNER BUSINESS DECISION`
- **Status:** `APPROVED; NOT IMPLEMENTED`
- **Source:** the owner, answers of 2026-10-05; answers 10, 11 and 18 were added or changed by the owner on 2026-10-20 after the conflict report of docs-only rules update 1. Recorded on 2026-10-21 in docs-only rules update 1b (ops/V1_056_TAKEOVER.md section 8). V1-056 stays paused before slice 11. Nothing is built by this entry, and V1-059 and V1-060 are not planned by it.
- **Resolves:** `OOD-DEPLOY-001` and `OOD-TEST-002` (answers 1 to 5); `OOD-DEPLOY-003` for V1 (answer 6); `OOD-DB-001` (answer 11); `OOD-DB-003` (answer 10); `OOD-DB-004` (answer 12); `OOD-DB-005` (answer 9). **Partly resolves:** `OOD-DEPLOY-002` (answer 7): the computer name, its address and the certificate method stay open; they do not block V1-059.
- **Backup and recovery (answers 1 to 5):** (1) Recovery point: at most 1 hour of data loss; backups run every hour. (2) Recovery time: the system works again within 1 working day. (3) Retention: hourly copies are kept 2 days, daily copies 30 days, monthly copies 12 months; the last good copy is never deleted (DEPLOY-043). (4) Off-host copies: a daily encrypted copy to an external drive or to a second computer in the office, and a weekly encrypted copy kept outside the building. No cloud storage service is used. (5) Restore test: a full restore test every 3 months and before every release.
- **Deployment (answers 6, 7, 8 and 17):** (6) Remote access is off in V1; the system is reached only on the office network (DEPLOY-015, SEC-058). (7) Production runs on a separate small computer in the office, used only for this system; it is not the development Mac mini. (8) The critical alerts of the DEPLOY-051 list go by Telegram message to the Owner and the Manager, and the health page shows a warning. An alert carries no Customer data. The Telegram bot token is a secret: V1-059 uses a placeholder only, and the token is never put in the repository or in a log. This adds one outbound connection, to Telegram, to the DEPLOY-016 allowed list. Telegram is optional in the SEC-059 sense: when a message cannot be sent, the system keeps working and the health page warning stays. (17) Technical (operational) logs are kept 90 days. Audit and money history are kept forever (DEPLOY-052).
- **Meter units (answer 9):** electricity in kWh, water in cubic metres (m3).
- **Document numbers (answer 10):** Invoices, Receipts and Refunds are numbered with a type code, the 2-digit year and a 4-digit running number, with no dashes or spaces, for example `INV260001`. Type codes: `INV` for an Invoice, `RCP` for a Receipt, `RFD` for a Refund. The running number restarts at 0001 each year, separately for each type. The year is the year of the issue date (Invoice) or of the confirmation date (Receipt, Refund) in the Property's local time, `Asia/Phnom_Penh`. If 9999 is reached in one year, the number grows to 5 digits (for example `INV2610000`) instead of failing. Numbers are never reused.
- **Drafts (answer 10a):** the number is given only when the record is issued or confirmed. A draft carries only an internal draft reference, which is never printed and never shown to a Customer. This replaces the DB-INV-001 rule that every Invoice, DRAFT included, has an `invoice_number`, and staff no longer type a `refund_number` on a Reservation Deposit Refund draft (docs/005, V1-056 slice 3b).
- **Payment Number (answer 10b):** a Payment has one Receipt, and the Payment Number is that Receipt's number (for example `RCP260001`). This replaces the separate Payment Number of BR-PAY-017 and DB-PAY-003 (today `PAY-` followed by the Payment id). Checked before recording: a Payment cannot have more than one Receipt today; `receipts.payment_id` is `UNIQUE` (DB-RECEIPT-001) and the Receipt is written in the Payment's own confirmation transaction.
- **Duplicate Customers (answer 11):** a new Customer field "ID number / Passport number". The owner approves this new personal-data field (SEC-006). A Customer with the same ID number as another Customer is refused; staff must use the existing Customer. The same phone number or the same email address as another Customer shows a warning, and staff may still save; the existing `confirmed_distinct` flow stays. The ID number never appears in exports (the owner's V1-057 answer 6, not yet recorded) or in the top bar search (UI-010).
- **Meter serial numbers (answer 12):** a serial number is unique across all Meters of the Property, whatever the Utility Type. Staff enter the serial printed on the Meter. If a Meter has no printed serial, staff enter a Property code instead (for example `EL-U101` or `WA-U101`), and it must still be unique. A replaced Meter keeps its serial in history, and that serial cannot be used again.
- **Release gate, V1-060 (answers 13 to 16):** (13) The release candidate has no flaky tests and no open security warnings. A flaky test is fixed, not run again until it passes. This includes TEST-FE-087, TEST-FE-128, TEST-FE-488, the DL-067 `LockNotAvailable` full-run failure and the `braces` advisory (DL-067). The run rule that reruns the known lock failure once during a sub-slice stays for development work only; it does not apply to the release candidate. (14) Scope fact: one installation manages one Property with under 100 Units (the owner has 23 today; BR-PROP-001). The speed test uses 300 Units with 10 years of made-up history. (15) Before V1-060 is done, the Owner or the Manager runs one test session with made-up data, following a short written script: reserve, sign, move in, bill, pay, move out, settle. V1-060 is not done until the owner says the session passed. (16) A new version follows V1-060: V1-061 "go-live data", which loads the current Units, tenants, Leases, deposits held and unpaid balances on day one. It needs its own short owner rules review before it starts. It is not planned now, and ops/V1_ROADMAP.json and scripts/validate-v1-roadmap.py are not changed for it yet.
- **DL-067 same-dates Utility gap (answer 18):** the list of unbilled periods plus the staff catch-up command is not enough. Before V1-060, the scheduled billing worker bills a `LATE_AFTER_SUCCEEDED_RUN` period by itself. The list (`app.utility_unbilled_periods`, `GET /properties/{id}/unbilled-utility-periods`) stays as a safety check. This replaces the DL-067 slice 7b rule that late periods are billed only by explicit staff action, never by an automatic run, and the matching DB-UTIL-013 and docs/005 sentences, for `LATE_AFTER_SUCCEEDED_RUN` periods only; a `NOT_MOVED_IN` period is still billed only by the explicit catch-up command. Placed on the V1-056 slice 12 list in ops/V1_056_PLAN.md: the plan has no V1-060 list, and slice 12 comes before the V1-056 push and so before V1-060.
- **Transition:** records made before these rules keep their recorded numbers and values; history is never rewritten.
- **Rules changed (matching lines, each "Amended by DL-071"):** docs/002 BR-CUST-002, BR-PAY-017, BR-RECEIPT-002, BR-UTIL-006; docs/003 PR-CUST-002, PR-PAY-017, PR-RECEIPT-002, PR-UTIL-006; docs/004 DB-CUST-001, DB-INV-001, DB-PAY-003, DB-RECEIPT-001, DB-REFUND-001, DB-UTIL-001, DB-UTIL-013, TCD-DB-001, TCD-DB-003, TCD-DB-004, TCD-DB-005; docs/005 the slice 3b Reservation Deposit draft route and the unbilled Utility periods note; docs/007 TEST-113, TEST-115, OOD-TEST-002; docs/008 SEC-041, SEC-058, SEC-059; docs/009 DEPLOY-015, DEPLOY-016, DEPLOY-043, DEPLOY-045, DEPLOY-047, DEPLOY-051, DEPLOY-052, OOD-DEPLOY-001, OOD-DEPLOY-002, OOD-DEPLOY-003; docs/010 DL-067 and the section 11.1 table; ops/V1_056_PLAN.md slice 12.
- **Answered (owner, 2026-10-21, docs-only rules update 1c):** the ID number / Passport number is required for every Customer. Two ID numbers are the same when they match after removing spaces and dashes and ignoring capital letters. The owner also confirmed answer 18 on the V1-056 slice 12 list, with `NOT_MOVED_IN` periods still catch-up only.
- **Build in:** V1-059 builds answers 1 to 12 and 17: the backup job (hourly, the three retention classes, never the last good copy), the off-host copy and restore-test procedures, the deployment configuration and `scripts/validate-deployment-config.py` (remote access off, the Telegram host on the egress list, a placeholder bot token), alert routing to Telegram and the health page warning, 90-day log rotation; the number generator (per type and year, `Asia/Phnom_Penh`, growing past 9999) with a nullable `invoice_number` and an internal draft reference while DRAFT, the `RENT-` and `UTIL-` numbers in `billing_run.py`, the `PAY-` number in the Payment confirmation function, the Receipt number trigger, the Refund number writers, and the staff-typed `refund_number` in `reservation_api.py`, `reservation_deposit_draft.py`, `reservation.py`, `deposit_api.py` and their screens; the Customer ID number column with its unique check, `customer.py`, `customer_api.py`, `customerClient.ts` and `CustomerManagement.tsx`, kept out of exports and the top bar search; the Meter serial check across the Property including replaced Meters, and the kWh and m3 unit configuration and fixtures. The unique checks on the ID number and the Meter serial are tightening changes and need the owner's go-ahead at V1-059 planning. V1-060 builds answers 13 to 15: the fixes of TEST-FE-087, TEST-FE-128, TEST-FE-488 and the DL-067 `LockNotAvailable` cause (the `braces` advisory fix, `typescript-eslint` 8.71.0 and its 35 lint errors, stays in V1-059 under DL-067), the 300-Unit speed test with its made-up data, and the owner test script and session. V1-061 builds answer 16 after its owner rules review. V1-056 slice 12 builds answer 18: the scheduled Utility run in the billing worker (`billing_run.py` and the worker's Utility run) bills a `LATE_AFTER_SUCCEEDED_RUN` period by itself, with tests; the unbilled list and the catch-up command stay.
- **Decision date:** 2026-10-05 (answers 10, 11 and 18: 2026-10-20).
- **Amended by DL-075 (owner, 2026-10-20; docs-only rules update 2b, part 2):** the `INV`, `RCP` and `RFD` letters and the next running number are Settings values (2 to 5 capital letters, all different; the number never goes back and carries on when the letters change during a year).

- **Type:** `OWNER BUSINESS DECISION`
- **Status:** `APPROVED; NOT IMPLEMENTED`
- **Source:** the owner, answers of 2026-10-04; answers 2 and 10 were changed by the owner on 2026-10-20 after the conflict report of docs-only rules update 1, and answer 10 again on 2026-10-21 after the conflict report of docs-only rules update 1b, which also confirmed the readings of answers 2, 5 and 11. Recorded on 2026-10-21 in docs-only rules update 1c (ops/V1_056_TAKEOVER.md section 8). V1-056 stays paused before slice 11. Nothing is built by this entry, and V1-057 is not planned by it.
- **Authorities:** API-073 to API-078, UI-022 to UI-024, UI-084 to UI-090, SEC-032, SEC-041, SEC-042.
- **Reports (answer 1):** all 9 reports of the UI-088 list are built. Each report shows only existing data: no forecasting, no new accounting groups, no new fees.
- **Overdue groups (answer 2):** 1 to 19 days, 20 to 29 days, and 30 days or more. For a recurring monthly Rent Invoice the days are counted from the 1st of the billed month, the same count as the day-20 and day-30 rules (BR-LEASE-026, DL-064), so it moves into "20 to 29 days" on the day its day-20 warning is due. Such an Invoice is overdue only from the 6th (BR-INV-051), so its first group really covers days 6 to 19. Every other Invoice, the Initial Rent Invoice included, counts from the day after its Due Date (BR-INV-051).
- **Export format (answer 3):** CSV only.
- **Export storage (answer 4):** a small export downloads at once and is not stored on the server. A large export (an export job, API-078) is kept 24 hours and then deleted.
- **Access (answer 5):** by default the Owner and the Manager get all reports, audit search, audit export and data export. Staff get only the operational reports, UI-088 reports 1 (Units and Reservations), 2 (Leases) and 7 (Readings: consumption without Rate or Invoice amounts), with no money totals, no audit search, no audit export and no data export. This is built as capabilities plus default role bundles; the bundles stay configurable (OOD-SEC-001). It limits only reports, audit search and export: it removes no permission Staff already have for their daily work screens, and the record timelines (API-073, UI-084) stay as they are. The capability names are proposed at V1-057 planning (a new capability needs an owner answer).
- **Customer details in exports (answer 6):** name, Unit and phone number only. No ID number, no address and no ID document.
- **Dashboard (answers 7 to 9):** "Leases approaching End Date" means 60 days or less before the End Date; "Reservations nearing expiry" means 14 days or less before the Expiration Date. The cards are the UI-023 list plus: Rent nonpayment day-20 warnings and day-30 defaults that are due, overdue Initial Rent, financial drafts waiting for approval, Deposits waiting for a decision, and Final Settlements not yet closed. Each card shows its as-of time and links to its filtered list.
- **Monthly money-collected summary (answer 10, changed 2026-10-20 and 2026-10-21):** the money received in a month (Payments by their received date), on these lines: Paid to Invoices, split by the DL-020 Invoice categories (from Payment Allocations); Late-payment Charges paid (DL-050 Charges, not an Invoice category); money that went to a Deposit; money kept as Customer Credit; Refunded from the Payment (Payment excess refunded straight from the Payment, BR-PAY-034, BR-REFUND-002, BR-REFUND-005); and money received but not yet allocated. A reversed Payment (DB-PAY-006; a returned Payment, DB-PAY-009, ends in such a reversal) stays in the month it was received, and its reversal is a minus line in the month of the reversal, so a past month's total never changes. The lines add up to the money received less reversals. This is a view of existing records, not accounting.
- **Currency (answer 11):** all totals are in USD, the accounting currency of DL-060, which is the approved basis UI-024, UI-090 and API-076 ask for. The Payment register also shows the KHR amount received and the exchange rate, as information only. KHR is never added to USD.
- **Audit export fingerprint (answer 12):** each audit export file gets a SHA-256 fingerprint, saved in the export's own audit event (UI-087).
- **No Customer statement (answer 13):** no printable Customer statement in V1-057.
- **Audit of exports and searches (answer 14):** every export and every audit search writes an audit event. Ordinary report views are not logged.
- **Rules changed (matching lines, each "Amended by DL-072"):** docs/005 API-074, API-076, API-077, API-078; docs/006 UI-023, UI-024, UI-085, UI-087, UI-088, UI-089, UI-090; docs/008 SEC-032, SEC-041, SEC-042.
- **Open (not decided by this entry):** whether the split lines of a past month show later Allocation changes (as of the report time) or are frozen at the month end; the month's total does not change either way. Proposed at V1-057 planning.
- **Build in:** V1-057, with its screens in the owner's design. Code to change then: `audit_api.py` (the audit search writes an audit event; capabilities for audit search and audit export separate from data export, SEC-032; record timelines keep today's access); new routes for API-076 (dashboard), API-077 (the 9 reports, the overdue groups, the money-collected summary, USD totals with KHR shown as information) and API-078 (CSV export jobs kept 24 hours, then deleted; small exports streamed and not stored; every export audited; the SHA-256 fingerprint in the audit export's event; Customer fields limited to name, Unit and phone); the default role bundles and the new capability names (owner answer first); the frontend client layer and the dashboard, report, audit search and export screens.
- **Decision date:** 2026-10-04 (answers 2 and 10: 2026-10-20; answer 10: 2026-10-21).
- **Amended by DL-079 (owner, 2026-10-20; docs-only rules update 2b, part 6):** four "Totals by Unit and month" reports come first, the nine reports follow in a new order with Utility consumption renamed, every report summary has a chart, the Payments report lines are set, and the Home page has eight cards and a grouped to-do list. Staff keep the same three operational reports by name (Unit occupancy, Lease dates, Utility consumption).

## DL-073 — Lease follow-ups: serious-breach deposits, Rent nonpayment letters, leaving and the Refund reminder

- **Type:** `OWNER BUSINESS DECISION`
- **Status:** `APPROVED; NOT IMPLEMENTED`
- **Source:** the owner, answers of 2026-10-20 to the Lease agreement points of DL-070; item 3c replaced and items 3a and 3b restated by the owner on 2026-10-21 after the conflict report of docs-only rules update 1b. Recorded on 2026-10-21 in docs-only rules update 1c (ops/V1_056_TAKEOVER.md section 8). V1-056 stays paused before slice 11. Nothing is built by this entry.
- **Links:** DL-070 (this entry closes its open item and records the Article 15.5 removal), DL-016, DL-032, DL-054, DL-064, DL-068, DL-069; BR-LEASE-022 to BR-LEASE-028, BR-RENT-030, BR-DEP-022 to BR-DEP-027.
- **Serious-breach deposits (item 1; closes the DL-070 open item):** a serious-breach termination (DL-070) keeps the Security Deposit, like any violation termination (DL-069, BR-DEP-026). The Pet Deposit pays pet damage and the rest is refunded (BR-DEP-027), unless the breach is a pet-rule breach, which keeps both Deposits (BR-DEP-022).
- **Rent nonpayment letters (item 2; the owner's explicit approval under BR-LEASE-024):** for a Rent nonpayment termination the day-20 Nonpayment Warning Notice (BR-LEASE-027) is letter 1, the day-30 default notice is letter 2 and the termination notice (BR-LEASE-022) is letter 3. A Rent nonpayment termination needs no other warning letters. The day-30 default notice becomes a letter the system records, like the day-20 Notice; the Serious Nonpayment Default condition of BR-LEASE-028 itself stays as it is, and nothing is automatic. Every other Customer violation still needs the three warning letters of BR-LEASE-024 (the serious-breach exception of DL-070 aside).
- **Late hand-back after the End Date (item 3a; office practice and fact, no rule change):** the Lease ends on its End Date, normally the last day of a month (BR-LEASE-031). Office practice lets the Customer hand back the keys up to the 4th day of the next month with no Rent and no fee for those days, like a late check-out at a hotel; this is not written in the Lease. The system has no 4th/5th cut-off: on any day after the End Date there is no holdover Rent, fee or penalty and no Rent Invoice for a month after the End Date (DL-014, BR-LEASE-017, BR-MOVEOUT-009, BR-RENT-010, BR-LEASE-031); the Lease stays SIGNED and the Unit OCCUPIED until staff record the termination and move-out (BR-LEASE-018, BR-LEASE-019, BR-MOVEOUT-008).
- **Money paid for a month after the End Date (item 3b; fact, no rule change):** no Rent Invoice can be issued for such a month (BR-LEASE-031; the billing run refuses with "Rent billing period is outside contractual Lease coverage"). Money paid for it stays as unallocated excess on its Payment (DL-030, BR-PAY-031). Staff allocate it to the final Invoices, or refund it, under the existing rules; it becomes Customer Credit only with the payer's authorization (BR-CREDIT-002), and a Refund of it is a Refund from the Payment to its payer (BR-PAY-034, BR-REFUND-002). The owner's earlier 3b wording, which used this money without asking the payer, is dropped.
- **Leaving before the End Date (item 3c, replaced 2026-10-21):** when the Customer chooses to leave before the End Date, or the Lease is terminated on a forfeiture ground of the BR-DEP-026 list (for example an unpaid Security Deposit or first Rent, a violation, or a serious breach), the Security Deposit is kept, and Rent already paid for the hand-back month is not refunded. When the Property ends the Lease with notice (Article 15.4 of the standard Lease agreement, BR-LEASE-022), or both sides agree to end it early, the existing rule stays: the Security Deposit pays the open debt and the rest is refunded (DL-032; owner answer to Q-2026-10-05-20 point 2). The DL-064 prorated credit for a moved-in unpaid-Initial termination stays as it is, and BR-RENT-030 stays as it is. In every case the Customer pays the monthly Utility Invoice (the one the office issues on the 25th; BR-UTIL-021 sets no fixed issue date), the final Utility Invoice and the cleaning charge. These are Invoices that exist under today's rules; this entry creates none, so a Lease that never moved in still has no Utility charge and no move-out charge (DL-064, DL-067).
- **Lease wording (item 3d):** Article 15.5 of the standard Lease agreement ("hands back the Apartment before the 5th of a month, no rent is owed") is removed from the Lease; the new Lease files are dated 2026-10-20. Article 2.5 stays the clause reference of the unpaid-Initial ground (DL-070). BR-RENT-030 is not changed by the removal: it comes from DL-068, not from the Lease.
- **Deposit Refund reminder (item 4):** the Lease says the deposit is refunded within 7 days after the final inspection and the final Utility Invoice. The system does not block anything, and DL-068 "no Refund deadline in the system" stays. While the Refund is not made, a to-do reminder shows "Refund due by" with the date 7 days after the later of the final inspection and the final Utility Invoice.
- **Renewal intent (item 5):** renewal intent 30 days before the End Date has no system record in V1. The 60-day "Leases approaching End Date" card (DL-072) is enough.
- **Landlord notice (item 6):** no change. BR-LEASE-022 already takes the notice from the signed Lease.
- **Rules changed (matching lines, each "Amended by DL-073"):** docs/002 BR-LEASE-024, BR-LEASE-028, BR-DEP-026, BR-DEP-027, BR-REFUND-014; docs/003 PR-LEASE-024, PR-LEASE-028; docs/010 DL-054, DL-068, DL-070.
- **Build in:** V1-056 slice 11 builds items 1, 3c and 4 with their routes and screens in the owner's design, together with the DL-070 serious-breach exception: `lease_termination.py` and the termination context (a serious-breach ground without the three warnings; "Article 2.5" as the default clause reference of the unpaid-Initial ground), the Lease forfeiture source `app.lease_deposit_forfeiture_source` (a serious-breach termination is a forfeiture ground; a pet-rule breach keeps both Deposits; the Pet Deposit pays pet damage first otherwise), and a read for the "Refund due by" reminder on the Final Settlement and Refund screens. The screen rebuild builds item 2 in the Rent nonpayment area: a recorded day-30 default notice (a new notice kind beside the day-20 Notice, with its route, client and screen), and a termination citing BR-LEASE-028 that asks for no warning letters beyond letters 1 and 2. Items 3a, 3b, 3d, 5 and 6 need no code.
- **Decision date:** 2026-10-20 (item 3c and the 3a and 3b wording: 2026-10-21).

## DL-074 — Administration, health, screen language, dates, devices, brand and accessibility (V1-058)

- **Type:** `OWNER BUSINESS DECISION`
- **Status:** `APPROVED; NOT IMPLEMENTED`
- **Source:** the owner, answers first given on 2026-10-04; answers 2, 4, 5, 7, 8 and 10 changed by the owner on 2026-10-20 to follow the owner's screen design. Recorded on 2026-10-21 in docs-only rules update 2, part 1 (ops/V1_056_TAKEOVER.md section 8). V1-056 stays paused before slice 11. Nothing is built by this entry, and V1-058 is not planned by it.
- **Authorities checked:** API-079 to API-081, API-099, UI-001 to UI-014, UI-091 to UI-103, UI-109 to UI-113, TEST-091 to TEST-095, SEC-021, SEC-022, DL-055 to DL-059, DL-072.
- **Resolves:** `OOD-SEC-001` (answer 1), `OOD-UI-001` fully (answer 8), `OOD-UI-002` and `OOD-TEST-001` (answer 7).
- **Default role bundles (answer 1):** the bundles stay configurable data, and a role name gives no power by itself (SEC-021). Owner: every capability, including user accounts, role bundles and settings. Manager: all daily work, approvals (`financial.approve`), reports, audit history, exports and the health page; no user or role administration. Staff: daily data entry only (Customers, Reservations, Readings, recording Payments, preparing drafts); no approvals, no administration, no audit, no export. DL-058 and API-099 stay: only the Owner may reset Manager and Staff accounts. Reading recorded with this entry: "no audit" and "no export" for Staff are the DL-072 limits (no audit search, no audit export, no data export); Staff keep the DL-072 operational reports 1, 2 and 7, and the record timelines (API-073, UI-084) keep today's access, as DL-072 answer 5 says.
- **Settings access (answer 2; replaces the 2026-10-04 answer "Owner only"):** the Owner, or a user the Owner ticks for "Settings access", may change the settings that part 2 of docs-only rules update 2 lists (Settings and Unit setup). Only the Owner gives or removes Settings access, and the Owner always has it. It is built as its own capability, given per user. "The Owner" here is the Owner account class (`account_class` `owner`), as in DL-058 and API-099, not a role name, so SEC-021 holds. Every settings change is dated, written to the audit history, and never changes an issued Invoice, Receipt or Refund.
- **Amended by DL-081 (owner, 2026-10-21; Settings access and the sign-in code):** any account that holds Settings access must use the sign-in code (MFA) at every sign-in, the same as Owner and Manager accounts. The Owner can give Settings access to a Staff account only after that account has set up its sign-in code; otherwise the give is refused with a plain message. No path may leave a Staff account with Settings access and no sign-in code.
- **Health page (answer 3):** the health page (UI-093, API-081 `GET /api/v1/operations/status`) is for the Owner and the Manager by default, through a capability in their bundles.
- **Screen language (answer 4; replaces the 2026-10-04 answer "English only in V1"):** Khmer and English in V1, with a ខ្មែរ / EN switch that changes every label. The app name stays in English in both languages. A native Khmer speaker checks the Khmer text before release.
- **Dates, times and riel (answer 5; replaces the 2026-10-04 answer "5 Nov 2026"):** dates are shown as dd/mm/yyyy everywhere, for example 05/11/2026. Periods are written 01/11/2026 - 30/11/2026. Times are 24-hour, in the Property's local time, `Asia/Phnom_Penh` (UI-095). Riel is written with ៛ after the number. The API keeps `YYYY-MM-DD` for calendar dates (docs/005); this is a display rule only.
- **Top bar search (answer 6):** the search box in the top bar finds Units, Customer names, phone numbers, and Invoice, Receipt and Refund numbers. It never searches or shows ID numbers (DL-071). Leases and Reservations are found by their Unit; a Payment is found by its Receipt number (the Payment Number, DL-071).
- **Devices (answer 7; replaces the 2026-10-04 answer "phones and tablets for viewing and confirming only"):** full work on desktop, laptop and iPad, in both directions (portrait and landscape), with touch targets at least 44px tall, in the latest Chrome, Edge and Safari (Safari on iPad included). Phones are for viewing and confirming, but every screen must still display on a phone. UI-101 is updated to match.
- **Brand (answer 8):** the CHETANA brand kit (logo, colours and fonts) as in the owner's design file DESIGN.md, which comes into the repository with the screen rebuild. The app name is "CHETANA Residence Management" (owner decision 2026-10-12) wherever the app names itself. Technical names (the repository, folders, the `property_rental` package, the database, environment variables, job names) do not change, and neither do the document titles of docs/001 to docs/010. No screen is changed by this entry.
- **Accessibility target (answer 9):** WCAG 2.2 level AA.
- **Reasons for actions (answer 10):** free text, with one exception: reducing or waiving a late-payment charge uses one of three fixed reasons plus a required "What happened" text (docs-only rules update 2, part 3, answer 4). Today's staff-entered reason fields, including the Reservation `reason_code` (a non-blank text of at most 100 characters; `RESERVATION_EXPIRED` is set only by the expiry job), already take free text.
- **Facts checked before recording:** no default role bundle is seeded today (`access_admin_api.py` only lists, creates, updates and assigns bundles); `GET /api/v1/operations/status` and the top bar search are not built; the settings routes use `configuration.read`, `service_rates.manage`, `utility_rates.manage` and `exchange_rates.manage` (`configuration_api.py`). On screen today, calendar dates are shown as the API sends them (`YYYY-MM-DD`, for example `invoice.invoice_date`), and timestamps either raw (for example `occurred_at` in `CustomerLedgerEvidence.tsx`) or through `toISOString()` in UTC (`formatDateTime` in `App.tsx`); all labels are English; layout is one shared `styles.css` with two narrow-screen breakpoints (36rem and 600px).
- **Rules changed (matching lines, each "Amended by DL-074"):** docs/005 API-080, API-081; docs/006 UI-005, UI-007, UI-009, UI-010, UI-091, UI-092, UI-093, UI-095, UI-097, UI-101, OOD-UI-001, OOD-UI-002; docs/007 TEST-094, OOD-TEST-001; docs/008 SEC-021, OOD-SEC-001; docs/010 the section 11.1 table.
- **Build in:** the login slice builds answers 1 to 3 on the server: the default Owner, Manager and Staff bundles as seeded configurable data (`access_admin_api.py` and a migration that seeds the bundles), the new per-user Settings access capability that only the Owner account class may give or remove and that the Owner always has (the capability name is proposed at that slice's planning; which of today's `service_rates.manage`, `utility_rates.manage` and `property.manage` checks it replaces is proposed then too), and the health capability for `GET /api/v1/operations/status`; Owner-only resets stay in `administrative_recovery.py`. The screen rebuild builds answers 4 to 10 and the administration, Settings and health screens: a translation layer with Khmer and English labels for all 25 screen components in `frontend/src` (`App.tsx` and the 24 workspace and management screens), with the language switch in the shell; one shared date, time and money formatter in the client layer (replacing `formatDateTime` in `App.tsx`, the raw date and timestamp output in the 18 screens that show dates, and the `toLocaleString("en-US")` and `Intl.NumberFormat("en-US")` money formatting in `CustomerManagement.tsx`, `DepositManagement.tsx`, `LeaseManagement.tsx` and `ReservationManagement.tsx`, with ៛ after riel amounts in the 7 screens that show KHR); `styles.css` and every screen layout for desktop, laptop and iPad in both directions with 44px touch targets and phone display; the CHETANA brand kit from DESIGN.md and the app name in the shell, the page title and printed documents; the top bar search (a new read route and client); WCAG 2.2 AA checks in the accessibility tests; free-text reason fields. V1-058 itself is planned only when the owner sends it.
- **Decision date:** 2026-10-04 (answers 2, 4, 5, 7, 8 and 10: 2026-10-20).

## DL-075 — Settings and Unit setup: billing calendar, Reservation limits, Payment Methods, numbers, Rates, Services, cleaning rates and Unit lists

- **Type:** `OWNER BUSINESS DECISION`
- **Status:** `APPROVED; NOT IMPLEMENTED`
- **Source:** the owner, answers of 2026-10-17; the conflicts reported in docs-only rules update 2 were answered by the owner on 2026-10-20. Recorded on 2026-10-21 in docs-only rules update 2b, part 2 (ops/V1_056_TAKEOVER.md section 8). V1-056 stays paused before slice 11. Nothing is built by this entry.
- **Authorities checked:** UI-091 to UI-093, BR-SVC-001 to BR-SVC-015, BR-RES-001 to BR-RES-022, BR-UNIT-001, BR-UNIT-014, BR-MONEY-005 to BR-MONEY-008, DB-PROP-001, DB-SVC-001 to DB-SVC-003, DB-LEASE-007, DB-UTIL-005, DB-PAY-001, DL-065, DL-071 (document numbers), DL-074 (Settings access).
- **Replaces on purpose (owner):** the values below change from "fixed in the business rules" to "set in Settings", with today's values as the defaults: the 25th issue day (BR-RENT-008, BR-SVC-011, DL-018), the 5th Due Date day of Rent and monthly Utility Invoices (BR-RENT-009, BR-UTIL-022, DL-018, DL-023), the configured "days after issue" (BR-INV-018, DB-PROP-001), the 10 percent late-payment rate (BR-RENT-029, BR-INV-052, BR-INV-053), the 21-day first Reservation expiry (BR-RES-006), the 14-day extension (BR-RES-008, DL-005), the 20 percent suggested deposit (BR-DEP-003, DL-008) and the `INV`, `RCP` and `RFD` letters of DL-071. Unit Types become a Settings list, which replaces the four fixed types of BR-UNIT-001. BR-SVC-001 is widened: Services are added in Settings (answer 8), not only by a separate Owner-approved rule.
- **Who may change Settings:** the Owner, or a user the Owner ticks for "Settings access" (DL-074 answer 2). Every change is dated, written to the audit history, and never changes an issued Invoice, Receipt or Refund.
- **Billing calendar (answer 1):** the reading day (default the 24th), the issue day (default the 25th), the Due Date day for Rent and Utilities (default the 5th), the days after issue for other Invoices (default 7, from 1 to 90, as DB-PROP-001 and the built migration already allow), and the late-payment charge rate. A day of the month is from 1 to 28, and the issue day comes after the reading day. The late-payment rate is a whole percent from 0 to 10 (default 10), because Lease Article 2.3 allows up to 10 percent.
- **When a change starts (answer 2):** a new reading day, issue day, Due Date day or late-payment rate starts with the next billing month. A new "days after issue" applies at once to Invoices issued after the change, as DB-PROP-001 says today. An issued Invoice never changes.
- **Reservations (answer 3):** the longest first expiry (default 21 days), the one extension (default at most 14 days) and the suggested deposit (default 20 percent). New values apply only to new Reservations.
- **Payment Methods (answer 4):** Payment Methods are added, edited and turned off in Settings. Each method says whether it needs a reference. A method used on a Receipt is never deleted, only turned off. At least one method stays on. Only methods that are on can be chosen (BR-PAY-006).
- **Riel rate (answer 5):** no change to BR-MONEY-005 to BR-MONEY-008: the automatic ABA Sell rate plus 0.5 percent, rounded up; manual entry only when the automatic rate fails, with a reason. Receipts already made keep their rate.
- **Numbers (answer 6):** Settings hold the letters for Invoice, Receipt and Refund numbers (2 to 5 capital letters, all three different; defaults `INV`, `RCP`, `RFD`) and the next running number, which can never go back. When the letters change during a year, the running number carries on (for example `INV260041`, then `CHI260042`). The rest of the format stays as DL-071 says.
- **Utility Rates (answer 7):** Utility Rates stay effective-dated (UI-091), and a new Rate starts on a reading day. The rate selection of BR-UTIL-015 and BR-UTIL-017 (the Rate effective on the Invoice generation date) stays.
- **Services (answer 8):** a Service has a name in English and in Khmer, a Service type and a monthly rate. A new rate starts on the first day of a later month, and issued Invoices keep the old rate. A new name shows only on new Invoices. A Service type is either "Only one per Lease" or "One or more per Lease" (for example two Trash Collection Services, of which a Lease takes only one). Changing a type to "Only one per Lease" is refused while a Lease holds two Services of that type. A type that has Services cannot be removed. Trash Collection is chosen by default on a new Lease.
- **Move-out cleaning rates (answer 9):** DL-065 stays: the cleaning charge is made on every move-out, and a Manager may reduce it with a reason. The per-Unit rate of BR-UNIT-014 and `app.unit_cleaning_rates` stay as built. The Settings screen sets one rate for a group of Unit Types (add, edit, remove), and the app writes that rate to every Unit of those types as a dated per-Unit rate. Each Unit Type is in exactly one rate group. A Unit Type that has Units must always be in a rate group. A new Unit gets the rate of its Unit Type.
- **Unit setup lists (answer 10):** Floors, Unit Types, Views, Kitchens and Room features (Balcony and any feature the Owner adds). New Unit and Update Unit pick from these lists. An item used by a Unit cannot be removed.
- **Fixed, not in Settings (answer 11):** the late check-out grace (keys back by the 4th after the End Date, DL-073); the Lease Start Date plus 5 days items (the Initial Rent Due Date and the rest of the Security Deposit and Pet Deposit: BR-RENT-009, BR-DEP-006, BR-DEP-010, BR-LEASE-005, Lease Article 2.5); the day-20 and day-30 letters and the DL-072 overdue groups, counted from the 1st of the billed month (BR-LEASE-026, DL-064); the day 20 and day 21 split of the first Rent period (BR-RENT-005, BR-SVC-012); move-out charges and the final Utility Invoice, due 7 days after issue (Lease Article 14.3), whatever the "days after issue" setting says; and the Reservation extension window of BR-RES-007.
- **Late-payment rate (answer 12):** a new late-payment rate applies to charges added after the change, for every Lease, and is never above 10 percent.
- **Readings recorded with this entry (the owner may correct them):** (a) Answers 2 and 12 read together: a new late-payment rate starts with the next billing month and from then on applies to every charge added, for every Lease. Which day starts "the next billing month" (the 1st of the next calendar month, or the next issue day) is not decided here; it is proposed at the screen rebuild planning. (b) BR-RENT-030 (hand-back before the 5th) is a hand-back cut-off, not a Due Date day, and is not in the answer 1 list, so it stays fixed at the 5th. (c) Answer 11's 7 days replace the configured number of days of BR-INV-018 for the move-out cleaning charge (`MISCELLANEOUS_CHARGES`), move-out Damage Charges (`DAMAGE_CHARGES`) and the final Utility Invoice; other one-time Miscellaneous charges follow the setting. The authorized Due Date override with a mandatory reason (BR-INV-018) is not changed. (d) The Unit Types list holds residential types only: "Commercial Unit is not supported" (BR-UNIT-001, DL-001) stays. (e) Whether a single Unit's cleaning rate may still be set apart from its rate group is not decided here; it is proposed at the screen rebuild planning.
