## DL-076 — Automatic late-payment charge, its reduction or waiver, payment order and the Receipt "Paid for" table

- **Type:** `OWNER BUSINESS DECISION`
- **Status:** `APPROVED; NOT IMPLEMENTED`
- **Source:** the owner, answers of 2026-10-17 18:31 and 19:23; the conflicts reported in docs-only rules update 2 were answered by the owner on 2026-10-20. Recorded on 2026-10-21 in docs-only rules update 2b, part 3 (ops/V1_056_TAKEOVER.md section 8). V1-056 stays paused before slice 11. Nothing is built by this entry.
- **Replaces on purpose (owner):** DL-050 (no automatic charge; one management decision per Invoice); the run rule "Nothing automatic" of ops/V1_055_RUN_RULES.md for this one job only, as DL-071 answer 18 did for the billing worker; and the DL-029 sentence "Late-payment Charges are separate obligations and are not silently inserted into the default Invoice FIFO". It changes BR-INV-052 to BR-INV-055, BR-LATE-001 to BR-LATE-003, BR-PAY-040 and OOD-BR-003 where they differ, with the matching lines in BR-RENT-029, BR-INV-051 and docs/001. BR-LATE-005 with the Q-2026-10-07-38 amendment stays, BR-CREDIT-014 stays, and the rest of DL-029 stays.
- **Automatic charge (answer 1):** at 00:00 Property time (`Asia/Phnom_Penh`) on the first day after an Invoice's Due Date, if any of it is unpaid, the app adds a late-payment charge by itself: the Settings rate (DL-075; default 10 percent) of the amount unpaid at that moment, rounded half-up to the cent (BR-MONEY-012). No Manager decision is needed. It applies only to the Invoices that may carry a charge today: issued Invoices (not DRAFT or VOID) with an unpaid balance, linked to a SIGNED or TERMINATED Lease. That covers recurring Rent with its Service lines, monthly and final Utility, Damage and Miscellaneous (the move-out cleaning charge included). It never applies to the Initial Rent Invoice (BR-INV-051), to an Invoice with no Lease, or to the charges themselves (BR-LATE-006). The list is not widened.
- **One charge (answer 2):** one charge per Invoice. Money paid later does not change it (BR-INV-054).
- **Its own record (answer 3):** the charge is its own record. It is not an Invoice and not a line on any Invoice. It is payable at once and is part of what the Customer owes (BR-LATE-001, BR-LATE-002).
- **Reduce or waive (answer 4):** the Owner or a Manager may reduce or waive a charge, only after the Customer complains that the charge is wrong because of a staff mistake. The amount can only go down. Each change needs one of three fixed reasons ("Staff recorded the payment on the wrong Invoice", "Paid on time but recorded late", "Other staff mistake") and a required "What happened" text (DL-074 answer 10). A charge that is already paid may still be reduced or waived, as BR-LATE-005 allows today; paid money above the new amount goes to Customer Credit under BR-CREDIT-014. History keeps every change.
- **Payment order (answer 5):** oldest Due Date first, and a late-payment charge is paid right after its own Invoice, before newer Invoices. Staff change the order only when the Customer names what to pay (BR-PAY-024). This replaces BR-PAY-040, where staff ticked the charge by hand. Staff still see the ticks and confirm with Receive payment (DL-029). A third-party payer's money pays only the Invoices the payer names, with no automatic ticks (DL-029 stays).
- **Note on the next Invoice (answer 6):** while a charge is unpaid, next month's Invoice shows a note "Unpaid late-payment charge" with its amount, outside the Invoice total.
- **Receipt "Paid for" table (answer 7):** the printed Receipt has a "Paid for" table: each Invoice with its type, number and period (move-out cleaning and Damage Invoices included, as Invoice rows), a late-payment charge right after its Invoice, then Deposit, Customer Credit and money not used yet.
- **Readings recorded with this entry (the owner may correct them):** (a) "The Invoices that may carry a charge today" keeps today's refusals too: no charge is added on an Invoice of a Lease whose Final Settlement is closed (BR-SETTLE-012, migration `20261027_92`). (b) When the rounded amount is zero (a Settings rate of 0 percent, or a balance under 5 cents), no charge record is made, because a charge is always positive (BR-LATE-001). (c) "The Owner or a Manager" is given as a capability in the default Owner and Manager bundles (DL-074 answer 1; SEC-021: a role name gives no power by itself); the capability name is proposed at slice 11 planning. (d) Answer 4 changes today's path for a paid charge before closure: today a reduction or reversal of a paid charge reverses the now-excess allocations, and their value goes back to the Payment as money not used yet (DB-INV-009); after this entry that value becomes Customer Credit of the charge's Customer at once, as BR-CREDIT-014 does for a credit Adjustment and, after closure, for a corrected charge (Q-2026-10-07-38). After closure the post-settlement correction path of BR-LATE-005 stays.
- **Facts checked before recording:** the eligibility check of `app.late_payment_decision_snapshot_for_invoice` and the decision function (migration `20260831_37`: a Lease in SIGNED or TERMINATED, Invoice status `UNPAID`, Due Date passed, a positive balance, no decision yet; the 10 percent default as `floor((balance + 5) / 10)`); `default_rate_basis_points` `CHECK (= 1000)` in DB-INV-007 (migration `20260827_29`); `finalized_by`, `reason` and `authorization_reference` are `NOT NULL` on the decision; `late_payment_charges.payable_at` is the management confirmation time and `created_by` the confirming user (DB-INV-008); the closed-Settlement refusal on `late_payment_decisions`, `late_payment_charges` and `late_payment_charge_corrections` (migration `20261027_92`); BR-PAY-040 and `payment_allocation.py` allocate to a charge only when staff pick it.
- **Rules changed (matching lines, each "Amended by DL-076" or "Replaced by DL-076"):** docs/001 section 21.5, the two Late-payment Charge Decision entries and section 101 items 44 and 48; docs/002 BR-RENT-029, BR-INV-051, BR-INV-052, BR-INV-053, BR-INV-054, BR-INV-055, BR-LATE-001, BR-LATE-002, BR-LATE-003, BR-PAY-040, OOD-BR-003; docs/003 PR-RENT-029, PR-INV-051 to PR-INV-055, PR-LATE-001 to PR-LATE-003, PR-PAY-040; docs/004 DB-INV-007, DB-INV-008, DB-INV-009; docs/005 API-091; docs/006 UI-105; docs/007 TEST-123, TEST-124; docs/010 DL-029, DL-050; ops/V1_055_RUN_RULES.md (business rules line); ops/V1_056_PLAN.md (slice 11 list).
- **Build in:** V1-056 slice 11 builds the backend: the 00:00 job in `billing_worker.py` (one run per Property-local day, idempotent, the eligibility of answer 1 and reading (a), one charge per Invoice); DB-INV-007 reads the rate from Settings instead of `CHECK (= 1000)` (migrations `20260827_29` and `20260831_37`); a system actor for `finalized_by` and `created_by`; DB-INV-008 `payable_at` at the job time; a new append-only table for reductions and waivers (the three fixed reasons, "What happened", the actor, the previous and resulting amount; the amount only goes down), with the paid part released to Customer Credit under BR-CREDIT-014; the decision trigger (no manual decision any more); API-091 (no manual decision route; a reduce or waive route); `payment_allocation.py` (the charge right after its own Invoice in the proposal; no automatic ticks for a third-party payer); and the tests in `test_late_payment.py` that expect a manual decision, changed to the automatic charge. Any committed test whose name these answers make wrong is renamed under the standing rule (ops/V1_055_RUN_RULES.md, Renaming a test whose name became wrong). The screen rebuild builds UI-105 (the reduce or waive screen), the "Unpaid late-payment charge" note on the next month's Invoice and the Receipt "Paid for" table.
- **Decision date:** 2026-10-20 (first answers 2026-10-17).
- **Matching line added after recording (2026-10-21, same session):** docs/002 BR-AUTH-006 (the late-payment authorization text) was missed in the list above and now has its "Amended by DL-076" line.

## DL-077 — Receive payment in one step, Credit on issue day, the Reservation deposit and proof of payment

- **Type:** `OWNER BUSINESS DECISION`
- **Status:** `APPROVED; NOT IMPLEMENTED`
- **Source:** the owner, answers of 2026-10-13; the conflicts reported in docs-only rules update 2 were answered by the owner on 2026-10-20. Recorded on 2026-10-21 in docs-only rules update 2b, part 4 (ops/V1_056_TAKEOVER.md section 8). V1-056 stays paused before slice 11. Nothing is built by this entry.
- **Replaces on purpose (owner):** the UI-063 text "Payment confirmation does not auto-select Invoices" and the docs/001 section 90.9 text "Payment Allocation is intentionally manual". DL-029 and DL-030 stay, except the one DL-029 sentence that DL-076 replaces.
- **One step (answer 1):** money pays Invoices in the same save step in which it is received. There is no "match later" while the Customer owes anything.
- **Ticks (answer 2):** when the amount is entered, the app ticks Invoices oldest Due Date first, with each late-payment charge right after its own Invoice (DL-076 answer 5). Staff change the ticks only when the Customer names an Invoice (BR-PAY-024). Changing the ticks sets the amount to the ticked total. A third-party payer's money gets no automatic ticks (BR-PAY-026).
- **Confirmation and transaction (answer 3):** pressing Receive payment is the staff confirmation (DL-029, BR-PAY-020). One backend command saves the Payment and its Allocations as separate records (BR-PAY-019) in one database transaction. Today the Payment and its Receipt are saved in one transaction and each Allocation in its own (`POST /payments/{payment_id}/allocations`, API-059); this changes.
- **Money that waits (answer 4):** money waits on the Receipt only when it is more than everything owed, or when nothing is owed. Then the Customer chooses Credit or a refund (DL-030, BR-PAY-030 to BR-PAY-034). It is never called Credit before that choice (BR-PAY-031).
- **Credit on issue day (answer 5):** on issue day, "One tap" fills in the use of the Customer's Credit for the new Invoice, and staff confirm it (BR-CREDIT-006).
- **Reservation deposit (answer 6):** Make Reservation receives the deposit on a Receipt in the same save step. The Reservation becomes active when the deposit is received in full, meaning the explicitly accepted initial Security Deposit amount (BR-RES-004, BR-DEP-001, BR-DEP-002).
- **Proof of payment (answer 7):** staff may attach a photo or PDF (at most 5 MB) to a Payment. It is optional, kept with the Payment and never deleted, and only users who may see that Payment may open it. The rule is recorded now but is not built in V1-056 or the screen rebuild: it is built in its own later "file storage" step, after V1-056, with the SEC-063 controls (file name, storage path, malware checks). The run rule "No photo storage" stays until then. Adding `python-multipart` then needs the owner's yes. Until then the screens show no upload button.
- **Facts checked before recording:** `payment_confirmation.py` writes the Payment and its Receipt in one transaction (the Receipt number trigger); Allocations are separate commands under `payments.allocate` (API-059, `payment_allocation.py`); recording a Payment uses `payments.record`; the Reservation holding deposit is received on a confirmed Payment before the Reservation create uses it (V1-056 sub-slice 10i-4b); SEC-063 does not itself authorize an upload feature; no upload route or file storage exists.
- **Open (not decided by this entry):** which capability the one-step command checks, because `payments.record` and `payments.allocate` are separate today and DL-074 gives Staff "recording Payments"; proposed at the screen rebuild planning (a new capability or bundle change needs an owner answer). The separate allocation route (API-059) stays for money that waits and for paying again after a reversal.
- **Rules changed (matching lines, each "Amended by DL-077" or "Replaced by DL-077"):** docs/001 section 90.9; docs/002 BR-PAY-020, BR-PAY-031, BR-RES-004, BR-CREDIT-006; docs/003 PR-PAY-020, PR-PAY-031, PR-RES-004, PR-CREDIT-006; docs/005 API-057, API-059; docs/006 UI-063, UI-066; docs/008 SEC-063; docs/010 DL-029.
- **Build in:** the screen rebuild builds answers 1 to 6: one backend command (a new route beside API-057) that saves the Payment, its Receipt and its Allocations in one database transaction, built on `payment_confirmation.py`, `khr_payment_confirmation.py` and `payment_allocation.py` (the proposal with each late-payment charge right after its own Invoice, no automatic ticks for a third-party payer); the Receive payment screen (ticks, the amount following the ticked total, money that waits shown as not used yet until the Customer chooses Credit or a refund); the "One tap" Credit use on issue day on the Credit application route (API-063); and Make Reservation receiving the deposit on a Receipt in the same save step (`reservation.py`, `reservation_api.py`, `deposit.py` and the Reservation screens). The later file storage step, after V1-056, builds answer 7 (a Payment attachment table, storage, the SEC-063 controls, the access check, and `python-multipart` only after the owner's yes).
- **Decision date:** 2026-10-20 (first answers 2026-10-13).

## DL-079 — Reports: totals by Unit and month, report order, charts, the Payments report lines and the Home page

- **Type:** `OWNER BUSINESS DECISION`
- **Status:** `APPROVED; NOT IMPLEMENTED`
- **Source:** the owner, answers of 2026-10-14; the conflicts reported in docs-only rules update 2 were answered by the owner on 2026-10-20. Recorded on 2026-10-21 in docs-only rules update 2b, part 6 (ops/V1_056_TAKEOVER.md section 8). V1-056 stays paused before slice 11. Nothing is built by this entry, and V1-057 is not planned by it.
- **Adds to:** DL-072 (V1-057). **Authorities checked:** UI-023, UI-024, UI-088, UI-089, UI-090, PR-QUAL-005, DL-060, DL-072.
- **Four totals reports first (answer 1):** "Totals by Unit and month" come first: Total Income, Total Payment, Total Electricity and Total Water. Each is a table with years down the side (newest first, only years that have records), January to December across, and a Total for each year. A Unit filter; All Units adds every Unit together.
- **Total Income (answer 2):** each item counts in the month it is for: Rent in its Rent month, with its Service lines; a first Rent Invoice that covers two months is split by month; monthly Utilities in the month their reading period ends, and the final Utility Invoice in the month its period ends; Damage, Miscellaneous and cleaning Invoices in the month issued; late-payment charges in the month they are added; credit Adjustments as a minus in the month of the Invoice they reduce; VOID Invoices are not counted; a kept (forfeited) Security Deposit in the month it is kept. Deposits held are not income.
- **Total Payment (answer 3):** every Receipt counts on the day the money came in, deposits included. Receipt reversals and returned Payments are a minus in the month they happen. Refunds are not taken off here; they show in the Payments report. Total Payment matches "Money received" in the Payments report.
- **Total Electricity and Total Water (answer 4):** the amount (from the Invoice lines) with kWh or m³ (DL-071 answer 9). Each month is the reading period that ends on that month's reading day (DL-075; October is 25/09 to 24/10). Broken-meter estimates count in their period's month and are marked "estimate". A final short period counts in the month it ends. The month comes from the reading period, not the day a Reading was typed.
- **The other nine reports (answer 5):** they follow, in this order: Invoice register and balances; Payments and allocations; Utility consumption (renamed from "Utility consumption, Rate and Invoice history"); Customer Credit ledger; Deposit liability and disposition; Final Settlement register; Unit occupancy; Lease dates; Audit activity. These are the nine UI-088 reports of DL-072.
- **Charts (answer 6):** every report summary has a chart. Money charts are in USD only; riel payments count at their recorded USD value (DL-060, DL-072 answer 11). A report without money gets a count bar chart (for example occupied and empty Units each month).
- **Payments report lines (answer 7):** the Payments report shows where money went with the DL-072 lines: Paid to Invoices (split by Invoice category as DL-072 says, move-out cleaning and Damage included), Deposits, Customer Credit, Late-payment charges, Refunded from the Payment and Not allocated, with reversals as minus lines. There is no separate "Move-out charges" line. Paid to Invoices equals the Paid total in the Invoice register.
- **Access (answer 8):** the four new reports are money reports: Owner and Manager only (DL-072 answer 5).
- **Home (answer 9):** eight cards in two rows show counts and totals (for example occupancy, outstanding Invoices, unallocated Payments, broken-meter charges, failed jobs). The dated DL-072 items go in a to-do list grouped Overdue, Today, This week, Later: expiring Reservations, Leases near their End Date, missing Readings, day-20 and day-30 letters, overdue Initial Rent, drafts waiting for approval, Deposits waiting for a decision, open Final Settlements and "Refund due by" (DL-073 item 4). Each card and to-do shows its as-of time and opens its page. Any DL-072 count without a card goes in the to-do list.
- **Readings recorded with this entry (the owner may correct them):** (a) The four totals reports are owner-approved monthly views of existing records; they add no fee and change no record. The UI-088 sentence that reports do not authorize new accounting classifications, and DL-072 answer 1 ("no new accounting groups"), stay for everything else. (b) Staff keep the same three operational reports DL-072 answer 5 gives them, now named Unit occupancy, Lease dates and Utility consumption (without Rate or Invoice amounts); the DL-072 numbers 1, 2 and 7 referred to the old UI-088 order. (c) The first Rent Invoice is split by month along its own line components (the prorated start month and the full following month, BR-RENT-005, BR-SVC-012).
- **Open (proposed at V1-057 planning; not decided by this entry):** which eight cards exactly; the month in Total Income of a late-payment charge reduction or waiver (DL-076) and of a kept Pet Deposit (DL-073 item 1); and whether the charts need a package (no new package without the owner's yes).
- **Rules changed (matching lines, each "Amended by DL-079"):** docs/006 UI-023, UI-088, UI-089; docs/010 DL-072.
- **Build in:** V1-057, with its screens in the owner's design: the four "Totals by Unit and month" reads (API-077) with the month rules of answers 2 to 4 and the Unit filter, Owner and Manager only; the report order and the rename of answer 5; a chart on every report summary (USD only for money, count bar charts otherwise); the Payments report lines of answer 7 reconciled with the Invoice register Paid total; the Home page (API-076) with eight cards and the grouped to-do list; the frontend client layer and screens.
- **Decision date:** 2026-10-20 (first answers 2026-10-14).

## DL-080 — Mock-up choices and practice notes confirmed: Lease names, Manager actions, ledger, move-out labels, Settlement roles, Refunds, sign-in, printed documents and V1.1 items

- **Type:** `OWNER BUSINESS DECISION`
- **Status:** `APPROVED; NOT IMPLEMENTED`
- **Source:** the owner, choices and practice notes of 2026-10-20 from the owner's screen mock-up; the conflicts reported in docs-only rules update 2 were answered by the owner the same day. Recorded on 2026-10-21 in docs-only rules update 2b, part 7 (ops/V1_056_TAKEOVER.md section 8). V1-056 stays paused before slice 11. Nothing is built by this entry.
- **How recorded:** each item is confirmed as stated. A doc is changed only where the rules were silent (items 1, 2, 5 (the screen label), 7, 10, 12 and 13). Items 3, 4, 6, 8, 9 and 11 already match the current rules, so no doc changes for them.
- **(1) Lease name:** a Lease has no number. It is named by its Unit, for example "Lease · U204". Docs were silent; no Lease number exists in the code.
- **(2) Manager actions:** Sign Lease, Extend Reservation and Terminate Lease need a Manager. BR-AUTH-002 and BR-AUTH-005 asked only for "applicable authorization"; the capabilities (`leases.sign`, `reservations.extend`, `leases.terminate`) go in the default Owner and Manager bundles and not in the Staff bundle (DL-074 answer 1; SEC-021: a role name gives no power by itself).
- **(3) Customer ledger:** the Customer ledger lists Invoices and Receipts. Deposits and Credit show on their own lines and are not part of what is owed. This already matches BR-LEDGER-006.
- **(4) Move-out due dates:** move-out charges and the final Utility Invoice are due 7 days after issue (Lease Article 14.3). Already recorded by DL-075 answer 11.
- **(5) "Move-out" label:** "Move-out" is a screen label only, not a new Invoice category. In the records the cleaning charge stays `MISCELLANEOUS_CHARGES` and damage stays `DAMAGE_CHARGES` (DL-020).
- **(6) Final Settlement roles (checked in detail):** Staff prepare the Final Settlement; a Manager confirms it. This matches BR-AUTH-009 (its Amended by DL-068 and DL-069 line) and BR-AUTH-010: Final Settlement and its corrections are drafts that have no financial effect until a holder of `financial.approve` confirms them. In the V1-056 code the Settlement is started and its drafts are recorded under `final_settlements.prepare` (`app.start_final_settlement` and the draft recorders of DB-SETTLE-003 and DB-SETTLE-005), and only a `financial.approve` holder confirms (the 8e-3 confirm and every correction confirm). DL-074 answer 1 puts preparing drafts in the Staff bundle and `financial.approve` in the Manager bundle. Facts noted, not differences: no rule or code check requires the confirmer to be a different person from the preparer (an Owner or Manager holding both may do both; the test helper `tests/refund_test_support.py` confirms as the same person); no bundles are seeded yet (login slice).
- **(7) Refunds:** BR-REFUND-014 stays. Every Refund records a method and a reference note; for cash, the note says who took the money. Refund methods stay their own list (Cash, and Bank transfer (ABA or another bank); `app.refund_methods`), not the Payment Methods list.
- **(8) Voiding the last month's Rent:** stays a locked Manager action: the hand-back resolution (`app.resolve_hand_back_rent_invoice`, V1-056 slice 5) re-assesses under the Invoice lock and needs `invoices.void`, a Manager bundle capability.
- **(9) History searches:** every search in History is itself recorded in History. Already recorded by DL-072 answer 14.
- **(10) Sign-in (for the login slice; checked against SEC-010 to SEC-018 and UI-109 to UI-113):** after 5 wrong tries, the person waits 15 minutes. The wait message is the same whether or not the account exists (SEC-012, UI-109). The one-time password the Owner gives after a reset (DL-058, API-099) works for 24 hours and must be changed at the first sign-in; the new password follows the 15 to 128 character rule.
- **(11) Practice:** meters are read on the 24th, and the Utility Invoice is issued with the Rent on the 25th, due the 5th. This fits BR-UTIL-020 and BR-UTIL-022 and the DL-075 defaults.
- **(12) Printed Invoice (A4) and Receipt (A5):** Khmer above English, dates dd/mm/yyyy, 24-hour times, riel as ៛ after the number (DL-074 answer 5), Invoice spelled វិក្កយបត្រ everywhere, no address or phone in the header, the full-colour logo (DL-074 answer 8), the ABA KHQR code on the Invoice, and a reprint mark "REPRINT · ច្បាប់ចម្លង" with the reprint date (BR-RECEIPT-004). No VAT (docs/001 section 90.7).
- **(13) Not in V1 (V1.1):** "Paid on time", visits, birthdays, repair requests, routine Unit checks, and the printed Joint Inspection and Unit Check forms. The move-out inspection records already built stay in V1.
- **Differences from the V1-056 code (reported, nothing changed):** item 2: the capability checks exist, but no default bundle is seeded, so today any user given `leases.sign`, `reservations.extend` or `leases.terminate` may act; item 7: the reference note is free text and nothing asks a cash Refund for who took the money; item 10: `local_authentication.py` has a per-account and per-source attempt limiter with configurable limits and window, but no 5-tries and 15-minute values, no one-time reset password and no forced change at first sign-in; item 12: no printed Invoice or Receipt layout exists yet (UI-106 is a screen). Items 1, 3, 4 (DL-075 build), 5, 6, 8, 9 (DL-072 build) and 11 need no code change beyond the steps already named.
- **Rules changed (matching lines, each "Amended by DL-080"):** docs/001 section 90.5; docs/002 BR-AUTH-002, BR-AUTH-005, BR-REFUND-014; docs/006 UI-034, UI-036, UI-040, UI-048, UI-076, UI-106, UI-109, UI-112; docs/008 SEC-012.
- **Build in:** the login slice builds item 10 (`local_authentication.py` with 5 tries and a 15-minute wait per account, the same message for unknown accounts; a one-time reset password valid 24 hours and a forced change at first sign-in in the administrative recovery flow, `administrative_recovery.py`, with the 15 to 128 rule of `password_security.py`) and the bundle part of item 2 (Sign Lease, Extend Reservation and Terminate Lease capabilities in the Owner and Manager bundles only). The screen rebuild builds the rest: Lease names by Unit (item 1), the Customer ledger lines (item 3), the "Move-out" label (item 5), the cash Refund note hint (item 7), and the printed A4 Invoice and A5 Receipt (item 12, with the KHQR code and the reprint mark); item 13 is left for V1.1.
- **Decision date:** 2026-10-20.

## DL-081 — Login slice decisions: plan approval, default bundle lines, Settings access, one Owner, one-time password, wrong-try limit, password rule, Staff MFA, recent reauthentication, new routes, read capabilities and local HTTPS

- **Type:** `OWNER SECURITY DECISION`
- **Status:** `APPROVED; NOT IMPLEMENTED`
- **Source:** the owner, 2026-10-21: approval of the login slice plan (ops/V1_056_PLAN.md section 7, commit 2aabe67) and the answers to Q-2026-10-21-150 to Q-2026-10-21-160 (option (a) for all eleven, as recommended, with the notes below); answer G7 of 2026-10-20 (recorded with the plan). Recorded on 2026-10-21 in a fresh session before sub-slice L1a. V1-056 stays paused before slice 11. Nothing is built by this entry; each login sub-slice (L1a to L8) adds its "as built" line here.
- **Authorities checked:** DL-055 to DL-059, DL-074 answers 1 to 3, DL-075, DL-077, DL-080 items 2 and 10, SEC-002, SEC-012, SEC-013, SEC-018, SEC-021, SEC-073, SEC-074, API-079 to API-081, API-096 to API-100, UI-109 to UI-113.
- **Recording payments (G7, 2026-10-20):** the Staff bundle gets both `payments.record` and `payments.allocate`, because Receive payment records the money and pays the Invoices in one step (DL-077). This closes the DL-077 open item for the bundles; the one-step command itself stays in the screen rebuild.
- **Default bundle lines (Q-150 (a)):** Staff get `identity.read_self`, `customers.read`, `customers.manage`, `reservations.read`, `reservations.create`, `utility.read`, `utility_readings.record`, `payments.read`, `payments.record`, `payments.allocate`, `receipts.read`, `final_settlements.prepare`, the reads `leases.read`, `invoices.read`, `deposits.read`, `credits.read`, `refunds.read`, `customer_ledger.read`, `rent_nonpayment.read`, `configuration.read`, `units.read` and `property.read`, and `reservations.cancel`, `reservations.complete`, `leases.draft`, `lease_signers.manage`, `leases.inspect`, `leases.move_out`, `utility.calculate`, `receipts.reprint` and `refunds.create` (a Refund is only a draft until a `financial.approve` holder confirms it). Owner note: Staff get no action that moves money at once or changes a Customer's standing; Sign Lease, Extend Reservation and Terminate Lease stay Manager actions (DL-080 item 2), so `leases.sign`, `reservations.extend` and `leases.terminate` are in the Owner and Manager bundles only. Staff never get `financial.approve`, `invoices.void`, `audit.view`, `identity.manage_access`, `settings.manage`, `operations.status.read`, any export, `leases.warn`, `utility_readings.correct`, `utility_meters.manage`, `utility.estimate`, `invoices.create`, `invoices.issue`, `invoices.adjust`, `damage_charges.bill`, `deposits.manage`, `deposits.refund.qualify`, `reservation_deposits.refund`, `payments.reverse`, `payments.allocations.reverse`, any `credits.*` change, `late_payment.review`, the `rent_nonpayment.*` changes or `exchange_rates.manage`. The Manager bundle has every assignable capability except `identity.manage_access` (`property.manage` included); the Owner bundle has every assignable capability. (Changed by the Q-162 (b) answer below: `identity.manage_access` is in no bundle, so the Owner and Manager bundles both hold every bundle capability, `billing.generate` included by the Q-161 (a) answer.) The bundles stay editable data (SEC-021).
- **Settings access (Q-151 (a)):** the capability is `settings.manage`. Owner note: it is given per user, never in a bundle; the Owner always has it through the Owner account class (`account_class` `owner`). Only the Owner account class gives or removes it. It replaces `service_rates.manage` and `utility_rates.manage` everywhere, and `property.manage` on the Property update, the Property configuration and the one-time charge due-days setting. `property.manage` stays for Unit create and update and the per-Unit cleaning rate until the DL-075 Settings screens move the cleaning rate to rate groups. The two old names stay in the catalog with no route using them.
- **One Owner (Q-152 (a)):** exactly one Owner account, the bootstrapped one. The Owner creates Manager or Staff accounts only. The class sets the MFA rule (Manager required, Staff optional) and the default bundle given at creation; the Owner may change the bundle later. The class never changes; to change a person's class, disable the account and create a new one (history stays).
- **One-time password (Q-153 (a)):** the app makes the one-time password (random, about 20 characters, easy to read aloud), shows it once to the Owner and never again; it works for 24 hours (database clock) and must be changed at the first sign-in. A new Manager or Staff account gets its first password the same way. The reset keeps the "also reset MFA" tick. An expired one-time password gives the normal sign-in failure.
- **Wrong-try limit (Q-154 (a)):** counted per normalized username (unknown names included); the 15-minute wait starts at the 5th wrong try within 15 minutes; tries during the wait are refused without checking the password and add no time; a correct sign-in clears the count; wrong TOTP codes and wrong recovery codes count as wrong tries for that account; per source address, 20 wrong tries in 15 minutes start the same 15-minute wait for that address; the counts are kept in the database. Anyone who knows a username can make that person wait 15 minutes; for the Owner that is accepted (the Owner waits, or uses the emergency server procedure of DL-058).
- **Password rule and protected files (Q-155 (a)):** every new password (bootstrap, the forced change, later changes) follows one rule: 15 to 128 code points before and after NFC and the same local blocklist. The API reads the TOTP protection key and the blocklist from protected files whose paths are the settings `APP_TOTP_KEY_FILE` and `APP_PASSWORD_BLOCKLIST_FILE` (paths only). On the Mac mini the key file is `/usr/local/etc/prm/totp_protection_key` (root-owned, mode 0600), opened by a small wrapper that then runs the API as the owner's user. Owner note: only in sub-slice L3c may Claude Code open `.env.example`, to add the two path setting names with no values; the added lines are shown in the L3c report; a real value, key or password is never written into it. The password credentials migration (`20260817_03`), `config/deployment/identity-secret-contract.json` and `docs/DEPLOYMENT_IDENTITY_SECRET_SCAFFOLDING.md` stay closed.
- **Staff MFA (Q-156 (a)):** only the Owner (`identity.manage_access`) sets a Staff account's MFA to required or optional; a Staff member does not turn it on alone in V1; turning it off later is a reset with "also reset MFA".
- **Recent reauthentication (Q-157 (a)):** a fresh password and TOTP code, within the last 15 minutes, for resetting an account, creating or disabling an account, changing a bundle or a user's bundle, giving or removing Settings access, and turning a Staff account's MFA on or off. Money actions are not on this list; they keep their capability and draft checks.
- **Health capability and new routes (Q-158 (a)):** `operations.status.read` goes into the Owner and Manager bundles now; `GET /api/v1/operations/status` is built with V1-059. Owner note: approving the plan also approves three new docs/005 routes: `POST /api/v1/auth/password-change` (L4), `POST /api/v1/users/{user_id}/settings-access` and `POST /api/v1/users/{user_id}/settings-access/remove` (L2); each is written into docs/005 by the sub-slice that builds it.
- **Local browser sign-in (Q-159 (a), with an owner addition):** Vite serves the frontend over HTTPS with a certificate the owner makes once with the macOS `openssl` (kept in the ignored `.local/` folder) and forwards `/api` to the API; no download and no new package. Owner addition: the certificate covers both `localhost` and the Mac mini's local network name, so the owner can also open the app on an iPad on the same Wi-Fi; the L7 runbook says how to trust the certificate on an iPad.
- **Read capabilities (Q-160 (a)):** two new capabilities, `property.read` and `units.read`, in all three default bundles, checked with the Property scope on `GET /properties/{property_id}`, `GET /properties/{property_id}/units`, `GET /units/{unit_id}` and `GET /units/{unit_id}/timeline`. Owner note: L5 also adds the missing Origin and CSRF checks to `POST /properties/{property_id}/units` and `PATCH /units/{unit_id}`.
- **Billing runs by people (Q-2026-10-21-161 (a), owner, 2026-10-21, after the L1b-1 stop):** `billing.generate` is a bundle capability, in the Owner and Manager bundles and not in the Staff bundle; people keep starting a Rent or Utility billing run and reading its status (API-054, API-055). This replaces the plan's "`billing.generate` belongs to the billing service principal only and can never be put in a bundle"; the scheduled billing job keeps its own service principal.
- **User and role administration (Q-2026-10-21-162 (b), owner, 2026-10-21, after the L1b-1 stop):** `identity.manage_access` comes only from the Owner account class and is never in any bundle. This keeps DL-058: only the Owner resets Manager and Staff accounts. The Owner and Manager bundles therefore hold the same bundle capabilities; the Owner's extra rights (`identity.manage_access`, `settings.manage`, the resets) come from the account class.

- **Login sub-slice L1a, the account class (DB-AUTH-001, DL-056, DL-058, DL-059, Q-152 (a); migration `20270118_175`):** a new append-only relation `app.user_account_classes` (one row per classed account: `actor_id` (key, foreign key to `app.user_accounts`, ON UPDATE and ON DELETE RESTRICT), `account_class` (`owner`, `manager`, `staff`), `classified_at`, `provenance`); a partial unique index allows at most one `owner`; a class is never updated, deleted or truncated (23000, "user account class is immutable"); an `owner` or `manager` class needs the account's `mfa_policy_class` `required`, checked when the class is given (share lock on the account row) and after any update that leaves an account's MFA policy not `required` (23514, "an Owner or Manager account requires MFA"); an MFA policy is lowered only at READ COMMITTED (55000, "an MFA policy can be lowered only at READ COMMITTED"; security review round 1: under REPEATABLE READ the class check could read a snapshot older than a class given meanwhile); the migration classes only the actor named by the bootstrap closure (`owner`) and changes no row or column of `app.user_accounts` (the table gains one trigger); the bootstrap function inserts the `owner` class right after the account (one exact-text change; same signature, owner, ACL, definer flag and settings); `prm_runtime` reads the relation only. An account without a class cannot be found for sign-in (`PostgresLocalAccountRepository.find_by_username`), does not resolve for recovery (new `PostgresRecoveryAccountResolver`, which reads the stored class of an active account) and gets no grants (L1b). An old unclassified account is never classified by any function: the Owner disables it and creates a new account. `app.perform_account_recovery` is unchanged. Design changes (implementer's, under the design-change run rule; for the round 1 reviewers): (1) no check that every new account carries a class, because about 100 committed test set-ups insert accounts without one as the migration owner; fail closed as above instead; (2) a separate relation instead of the planned `account_class` column, because adding a column or a check to `app.user_accounts` needs an ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock and deadlocked the committed whole-chain upgrade test `test_v1_042_upgrade_front_door_gate_prevents_service_writer_deadlock` (targeted run T1); a new table with a foreign key and a new trigger take only SHARE ROW EXCLUSIVE on `app.user_accounts`, and DB-AUTH-001 already keeps assignments in separate relations. Both design changes were confirmed as needed and safe by the review round 1 independent reviewer. Not built, for later sub-slices (review round 1 notes): the L2 account-create function refuses the class `owner` and records who gave each class (SEC-075); L4 decides a class check of actor and target inside `app.perform_account_recovery`; the L7 runbook says never to run the bootstrap while a migration runs (a bootstrap call started before this migration could close the bootstrap without an Owner class; a closure check was not built because committed closure tests call the closure function for accounts without a class).
- **Updated tests (login sub-slice L1a):** the head-revision assertions now expect `20270118_175` (27 assertions in 15 modules); only the expected revision changed. The new PostgreSQL module `test_account_class_migration.py` runs last in `scripts/database-test.sh`.
- **Login sub-slice L1b-1, the capability catalog (SEC-001 to SEC-003, SEC-020, SEC-021, API-080, DB-AUTH-006; Q-151, Q-158, Q-160 and Q-161 (a), Q-162 (b); migration `20270119_176`):** L1b is split into L1b-1 (the catalog) and L1b-2 (role bundles, assignments and the grant reader). A read-only survey of every dotted string literal in `backend/src` and the migrations found 71 capabilities: 70 checked by the application and `rent_nonpayment.evaluate`, checked only by the database for the nonpayment evaluation principal; every other dotted literal is a request-digest, audit-action, log-event, message-type or function label. The new append-only `app.capabilities` holds those 71 and the four approved names `settings.manage`, `operations.status.read`, `property.read` and `units.read` (75 rows), each with one grant path: `per_user` for `settings.manage`, `owner_class` for `identity.manage_access` (Q-162 (b)), `service_principal` for `rent_nonpayment.evaluate`, `bundle` for the other 72, `billing.generate` included (Q-161 (a); review round 1 found that people start billing runs and read their status with it); the pair of capability and grant path is unique for a later bundle reference; a name is at most 128 characters and `added_at` is finite. No capability is renamed and no check changes. The application keeps the same catalog in `property_rental.access_control`; a unit test fails when the code uses a dotted string that is neither a catalog capability nor a listed label.
- **Updated tests (login sub-slice L1b-1):** the head-revision assertions now expect `20270119_176` (27 assertions in 15 modules); only the expected revision changed. The new PostgreSQL module `test_capability_catalog_migration.py` runs last in `scripts/database-test.sh`.
- **Login sub-slice L1b-2, role bundles, assignments and the grant reader (SEC-001 to SEC-003, SEC-017, SEC-020 to SEC-022, API-080, DB-AUTH-001, DB-AUTH-007; Q-161 (a), Q-162 (b); migration `20270120_177`):** `app.role_bundles` (the current name and version of each bundle of a Property; the name unique per Property whatever its capital letters, with no C0 or C1 control character and none of the listed invisible format characters (review rounds 1 and 3, Q-2026-10-21-163 (a)); an update changes only the name and raises the version by exactly 1; never deleted), `app.role_bundle_versions` (every version and its name, written by a trigger with the bundle) and `app.role_bundle_capabilities` (the complete capability set of every version; only catalog capabilities with grant path `bundle`, by a foreign key on the capability and its grant path; written only for the current version and only by the transaction that wrote it, checked by its transaction id and start time (security review round 1: a logical restore may reuse an old transaction id), so a recorded version never changes); `app.user_role_assignments` (at most one active assignment of a bundle to an account, checked under a lock at READ COMMITTED only) and `app.user_role_assignment_removals` (an assignment ends at most once, with a reason); who assigned or removed is a real account, null only for seeds (review round 1); the history relations are append-only. The definer reader `app.actor_capability_grants(actor_id)` gives an active, classified account the current capabilities of its actively assigned bundles with their Property, and `identity.manage_access` for every Property to the Owner account class only (Q-162 (b)); disabled, unclassified and unknown accounts get nothing; a removed capability or assignment stops at the next read. `settings.manage` is added to the reader by L1d and the object scopes by L2. The runtime role may only execute the reader. The application reads it through `PostgresCapabilityGrantReader` in `property_rental.access_control`, which refuses every grant when a name is not in the application catalog (fail closed). No writer function is built yet: L1c seeds the default bundles and L2 administers bundles and assignments, each through reviewed definer functions.
- **Updated tests (login sub-slice L1b-2):** the head-revision assertions now expect `20270120_177` (27 assertions in 15 modules); only the expected revision changed. The new PostgreSQL module `test_role_bundle_migration.py` runs last in `scripts/database-test.sh`. One historical expectation narrowed (run P1): `test_capability_catalog_migration.py::test_the_capability_catalog_is_append_only` now expects a `TRUNCATE app.capabilities` alone to be refused by the new foreign key from `app.role_bundle_capabilities` (`FeatureNotSupported`, "cannot truncate a table referenced in a foreign key constraint") instead of by the append-only trigger, which PostgreSQL runs only after that check; the test name and its other cases are unchanged, and the trigger's refusal is still checked by `test_role_bundle_migration.py` with both tables in one TRUNCATE.
- **Login sub-slice L1d, per-user Settings access (SEC-014, SEC-021, SEC-075, DB-AUTH-008; Q-151 (a); migration `20270121_178`):** L1c waits for Q-2026-10-21-164 (nine capabilities the Staff bundle answer does not name), so L1d is built first. `app.user_capability_grants` (only `settings.manage` with grant path `per_user`; who gave it, when and why; at most one active grant per account, checked under a lock at READ COMMITTED only; a removal takes the same lock, also at READ COMMITTED only) and `app.user_capability_grant_removals` (a grant ends at most once, with who, when and why) are append-only. The definer functions `app.give_settings_access` and `app.remove_settings_access` refuse unless the acting account is the active Owner account class (42501); a grant goes only to an active Manager or Staff account (22023); a second grant is refused (23505) and a removal without a grant (55000). Design change (review round 1, under the design-change run rule): a removal checks only the acting Owner, so the Owner can remove the Settings access of a disabled account (otherwise it could never be removed and would come back when the account is enabled again). The audit events of these actions (SEC-014, SEC-075) and their tests move to the L2 routes, which call the functions in the same transaction; the grant and removal rows already keep who, when and why. The reader `app.actor_capability_grants` is replaced (same signature, owner, privileges and attributes) so it also gives `settings.manage` for every Property to the Owner account class and to an account with an active grant; a removal takes effect at the next read and revokes nothing else. The application reader accepts the `per_user` grant path from now on. The routes and the recent-reauthentication check come with L2 and L3d.

Two L1b-2 expectations change with the approved plan (Q-151 (a): the Owner always has Settings access, and the reader gives it from L1d): in `test_role_bundle_migration.py::test_the_grant_reader_gives_an_active_classified_account_its_current_capabilities` the Owner also gets `settings.manage`, and in `test_access_control.py::test_the_grant_reader_groups_property_ids_and_refuses_names_it_may_not_give` `settings.manage` is now accepted instead of refused. One set-up changed for the new foreign keys: in `test_role_bundle_migration.py::test_a_role_bundle_name_is_unique_per_property_and_every_version_is_kept` the catalog TRUNCATE also names `app.user_capability_grants` and `app.user_capability_grant_removals` (both now refer to the catalog or to each other); the check and its message are unchanged. The new PostgreSQL module `test_settings_access_migration.py` runs last in `scripts/database-test.sh`.
- **Staff bundle, the nine unnamed capabilities (Q-2026-10-21-164 (a), owner, 2026-10-21, fresh session):** none of `deposits.dispose`, `deposits.correct`, `reservation_deposits.dispose`, `reservation_deposits.correct`, `reservation_deposits.override`, `refunds.correct`, `refunds.corrections.reverse`, `late_payment.charge_correction` and `late_payment.final_decision` is in the Staff bundle; they stay in the Owner and Manager bundles.
- **Login sub-slice L1c, the default bundles (DL-074 answer 1, DL-080 item 2, SEC-021, SEC-022, API-080, DB-AUTH-009; Q-150 (a), Q-164 (a), G7, Q-161 (a), Q-162 (b); migration `20270122_179`):** the definer function `app.seed_default_role_bundles(property)` makes a Property's default bundles once, at READ COMMITTED under a per-Property lock: "Owner" and "Manager", each with every catalog capability whose grant path is `bundle` at that moment (72 today), and "Staff", with exactly the 31 capabilities of the Q-150 (a) list (G7's `payments.record` and `payments.allocate` included; nothing of the "never" list or of Q-164), all at version 1; it records them in the new append-only `app.default_role_bundles` (one row per Property, so L2 can give a new account its class's default bundle even after a rename) and assigns the Owner bundle to the Owner-class account, if one exists, as a seed assignment. Reading recorded for the reviewers: the bootstrapped Owner is made before the Property (the Property's `created_by` must be an existing account), so "Owner: every capability" needs this seed assignment; Manager and Staff accounts get their default bundle at creation in L2 (Q-152 (a)). Seeding again returns the same bundles and changes nothing; a later catalog capability is never added to an existing bundle by itself. The migration seeds the Property that already exists (a fresh database has none). The Property setup (`PostgresPropertyConfigurationRepository.add`, the path of `property_setup_cli.py`) calls the function in the same transaction as `app.initialize_property` (implementer's reading: the plan named the command; the repository holds its transaction). The runtime role may execute the function only. The Python constant `STAFF_DEFAULT_BUNDLE_CAPABILITIES` holds the same 31 names. Review round 1: the Property setup checks the initialized row before the commit, so a failed seed leaves no Property behind; the seed writes no audit event (its rows keep time and provenance). Ordering note: the Owner and Manager bundles also hold `service_rates.manage`, `utility_rates.manage` and `property.manage` (every bundle capability), which the rate routes and the Property update, Property configuration and due-days setting check until L5 replaces them with `settings.manage` (Q-151 (a)); no build between L3a and L5 is used, and L5 tests that a Manager-bundle holder without `settings.manage` cannot change any of these five settings and can still create and update a Unit. Only the Staff constant was added to `access_control.py`; the three bundle names planned there stay in the migration (nothing in the code needs them yet).

- **Settings access and the sign-in code (owner rule, 2026-10-21, fresh session; amends DL-074 answer 2):** an account that holds Settings access must use the sign-in code (MFA) at every sign-in, like the Owner and Manager classes. The Owner gives Settings access to a Staff account only after that account has set up its sign-in code; otherwise the give is refused with a plain message. No path may leave a Staff account with Settings access and no sign-in code; a reset or removal path that needs the owner's choice gets a question. Readings recorded: removing Settings access revokes no session (as L1d); a Settings access removal by MFA off is in the audit event of the account change (`identity.account.updated` or `identity.account.disabled`, with the removed grant id), not a separate `identity.settings_access.removed` event. - **Hidden characters in names and reasons (Q-2026-10-22-169 (a), owner, 2026-10-22, fresh session):** Khmer keyboards put an invisible space (U+200B) between words, so the API removes U+200B from names and reasons before saving them (it never changes how the text looks), and refuses the other invisible characters that were still accepted (Q-169 gap (2): in names U+034F, the Hangul fillers and the invisible Khmer vowels U+17B4 and U+17B5; in reasons U+00AD, U+180E, U+FEFF, U+2060 to U+2064, U+FFF9 to U+FFFB and the tag characters U+E0000 to U+E007F). A character that normal Khmer typing needs (for example U+200C or U+200D) is not refused; a question is written instead. The rule applies wherever the login slice checks names or reasons (bundle names, usernames, display names, audit names and the administration reasons); a username that an administration function writes is NFC (a database check; before the first bootstrap, L7 makes the first-Owner bootstrap's username follow the same rule or refuses a username that differs) and the sign-in lookup uses the creation rule. Look-alike letters from other alphabets stay a practice point (the Owner reads new names on the account list). Other parts of the app with the same kind of check (for example Customer names) are not changed now; they are on the slice 12 list. Reasons keep no database character check (as in L2b-1). - **Login sub-slice L3a-1, password sign-in, the session read and sign-out (DL-055, DL-056, DL-057, API-096, API-097, SEC-010, SEC-011, SEC-015, SEC-016, DB-AUTH-004; no migration):** L3a is split into L3a-1 (this line) and L3a-2 (the actor resolver and its wiring). New `PostgresAuthenticationFlow` (`auth_flow.py`), used by `create_app` when `APP_DATABASE_URL` is set and no flow is given. Sign-in uses the existing `LocalAuthenticationService` (Argon2id, a dummy verifier for unknown names, one generic rejection) with a lookup that opens its own short connection, and the existing in-memory limiter as a coarse per-process flood guard (20 tries per username and 100 per source in 15 minutes; decided by Claude Code under the owner's 2026-10-22 rule; L3b adds the database count). An account with MFA policy `required` gets the phase `mfa_required` with an unstored pre-authentication token and no session (the challenge is unavailable until L3c); any other account gets an `app.browser_sessions` row that keeps only the sha256 digest of a random 32-byte token, which goes only into the session cookie, with a new CSRF token. `SessionView` and `SessionData` gain `display_name`. The session read answers only a live session of an active, classified account with MFA policy `optional` and records no activity (decided by Claude Code under the owner's 2026-10-22 rule: the shell reads the session to time its expiry); sign-out revokes the session when it is not revoked and before both expiries, whatever the account's state (reason `logout`, by its own account). A cookie over 128 characters is refused before hashing; `LoginRequest.username` is narrowed to 128 characters. Nothing secret or the username is logged; the session rows keep who signed in and out and when (the audit table needs a Property, which does not exist when the Owner first signs in). The runtime role already has every grant needed; no migration. Review round 1 (one independent and one security agent; no blocker): the session transaction checks the password again against the account's current verifier before it writes the session, so a password reset that committed after the first check leaves no session made with the old password (security); a reset that commits after that read and before the commit stays a narrow gap that login sub-slice L4 closes (binding, widened by review round 2: no password or sign-in code replacement and a session write that checked the old one may both commit, for example a lock taken by both in definer functions); every connection has a 5-second connect timeout; new tests: a session refused after its account is disabled or its MFA policy raised, a database that cannot be reached answers 503, the flood guard; note for L3b and L7: the flood guard and the wrong-try count key on the connecting address, so behind a reverse proxy every person shares one source (the proxy setup must pass the real address in a way the API trusts, or the source limit stays per proxy).

The new PostgreSQL module `test_auth_flow_migration.py` runs last in `scripts/database-test.sh`.
- **Login sub-slice L3a-2, the actor resolver (API-008, API-097, SEC-002, SEC-016, SEC-017, DB-AUTH-004, DB-AUTH-007; migration `20270127_184`, review round 1):** new `PostgresSessionActorResolver` (`session_actor.py`), used by `create_app` when `APP_DATABASE_URL` is set and no resolver is given (building it opens no connection; without a database everyone is still denied). On every request with a session cookie, in one READ COMMITTED transaction: the activity is recorded (`last_activity_at = statement_timestamp()`, skipped when a parallel request already recorded a later one), then the live session is read as the session read does (so a session revoked or expired meanwhile gives no actor), then the grants are read through `PostgresCapabilityGrantReader`; the Owner's object scopes are added to `identity.manage_access` and the `actor` scope of the actor itself to `identity.read_self`. No cookie, a token over 128 characters or no live session gives no actor (401); a database error or a capability the catalog does not know answers 503. Every connection of the sign-in flow, the resolver and the Owner's scope read has a 5-second connect timeout and a 5-second statement timeout. The activity is recorded only for a session of an active, classified account with MFA policy `optional`. Review round 1 (one independent and one security agent; the security agent found a blocker): from now on every request records activity, so a revocation (sign-out, and every Owner revocation: disable, Staff MFA raise, smaller bundle, assignment removal, explicit revocation, password and MFA resets) whose statement started before a parallel activity committed broke `CHECK (revoked_at >= last_activity_at)` and rolled back, and a person who kept using the app could stop their own revocation; design change under the design-change run rule, confirmed as needed and safe by review round 2: migration `20270127_184` (a relaxing change) replaces `app.protect_browser_session_lifecycle` (same signature, owner, privileges and attributes) so a revocation records `GREATEST(statement time, last activity)`; the sign-out guard and second statement planned for the L3a-1 round 3 binding are not built, because the trigger now covers every revocation path. Tests: a sign-out and an Owner revocation that each wait for the session row while a later activity commits record a revocation time equal to that activity (review round 2), and a session the resolver refuses gets no activity (review round 2). The ordering rule of L1c still holds: no build between L3a and L5 is used.

- **Wrong-try wait rule amended (owner, given 2026-10-23 in a fresh session as the rule amended on 2026-10-21; amends DL-080 item 10 and the "Wrong-try limit (Q-154 (a))" line above):** after 3 wrong tries in a row for one username the person waits 5 minutes; after 2 more wrong tries (5 in a row) the person waits 15 minutes; after that, every 2 more wrong tries mean another 15-minute wait, until a correct sign-in. The rest stays as Q-154 (a) says: counted per username, unknown names included; tries during a wait are refused without checking the password and add no time; a correct sign-in clears the count; wrong sign-in codes and recovery codes count; 20 wrong tries per source address in 15 minutes start a 15-minute wait for that address; counts kept in the database; the same wait message whether or not the account exists. Owner's example: Sokha types the wrong password 3 times at 09:00 and waits until 09:05; 2 more wrong tries then mean waiting 15 minutes. Reading recorded (Q-2026-10-23-176, recommendation (a), as built): "in a row" has no time limit; the count is every wrong try since the last correct sign-in. Rules changed (each "Amended by DL-081"): docs/005 API-096, docs/006 UI-109, docs/008 SEC-012; docs/004 DB-AUTH-011 added.
- **Login sub-slice L3b, the wrong-try count and the waits (DL-080 item 10 as amended above, Q-154 (a), SEC-012, UI-109, API-096, DB-AUTH-011; migration `20270128_185`):** three append-only relations (`app.sign_in_wrong_tries`, `app.sign_in_waits` with a check that a username wait is 5 or 15 minutes and a source wait 15 minutes, `app.sign_in_try_clears`) keyed by sha256 digests of the normalized username and the request source (pseudonymous; Q-2026-10-23-175 asks about a keyed digest and removing old rows); three definer functions, READ COMMITTED only, each under the username lock and then the source lock: the wait read, the record (a try during a wait records nothing and answers the wait) and the clear (answers an active wait and clears nothing; clears only for the active account whose normalized username gives the digest). `LocalAuthenticationService` asks for a wait after the in-memory flood guard and refuses without the lookup or the password check; every refused password check records one wrong try. `PostgresAuthenticationFlow` answers a wait with `AuthenticationRateLimited` (429 `RATE_LIMITED`, `Retry-After`, `no-store`); a correct password of an account that needs MFA is checked again for a wait under the locks before the MFA step (review round 1, security blocker) and neither counts nor clears; the session transaction no longer checks the password a second time: it compares the sha256 digest of the stored verifier the password was checked against with the one it reads (owner answer (a) to Q-2026-10-23-177, review round 3 blocker: a correct password that met a parallel wait answered one Argon2id check later than a wrong one), and then clears. Technical choices decided under the owner's 2026-10-22 rule: Q-2026-10-23-174. An account needs MFA when its MFA policy is `required` or it has an active sign-in code (the L3a-1 binding); its password-checked sign-in writes a challenge row (only the sha256 digest of the pre-authentication token, the purpose, for a `challenge` the active sign-in code it was made for (review round 1, security), the digest of the checked password verifier, the wrong-try digests; 5 minutes by the database clock; completed once) and answers `mfa_required`, or `mfa_enrollment_required` without a sign-in code. `complete_mfa` with `totp` opens the active enrollment with the protection key read from `APP_TOTP_KEY_FILE` (AES-256-GCM, the row's key identifier), accepts the code of the current or the previous 30-second step of the database clock, each step once and after the last used step, counts a wrong code as a wrong try of kind `sign_in_code` and answers a wait with 429; the right code, in one transaction, clears the count first, locks the enrollment, records the step, completes the challenge, compares the current password verifier with the checked one, and writes the session with an MFA proof (`mfa_assurance` `totp`). A session of an account that needs MFA is live (the session read, the actor resolver and its activity write) only with its proof. Without the key file the challenge answers 503; `recovery_code` stays unavailable until L3c-2c. Each runs in one READ COMMITTED transaction: the session check, then the per-account `pg_try_advisory_xact_lock`, so one account's codes are made once at a time (a parallel request answers 401 without hashing), then the other checks (for a regeneration the prior set locked; at most 5 sets of the account in 15 minutes, review round 2), then the slow hashing, then the writes (the prior set invalidated by the account itself, naming the replacement set, before the new set), then the session read again `FOR SHARE` and still proven with an active sign-in code. A parallel second set meets the new partial unique index `recovery_code_sets_one_live_per_actor` and answers 401. The flow writes the rows itself with the existing generator and verifier (the existing issuance and regeneration repositories commit on their own connection, so they cannot share the transaction that checks the session).

A `recovery_code` proof counts only while the sign-in code its challenge was made for is active (the L3c-2a binding: a sign-in code reset also ends recovery-code sessions, besides their revocation). The L3c-2c-1 binding on the code format (security S3: not 10 Argon2id checks per try, and a code easier to copy by hand) is set aside in part: the existing Argon2id codes are kept (Q-2026-10-24-182 point 1; one account's tries run one at a time, every try needs the password and a 5-minute sign-in step and is counted, at most 10 codes are read), confirmed as adequate by the round 1 security reviewer; a code easier to copy by hand stays open for L7 (before the first Owner's codes are printed). Review round 1: the wait is checked again under the try lock and a wrong code is counted before the lock ends; the proof needs the code's set to be live; the proof's code has a foreign key; the audit correlation id is in the decision log. Review round 2: the try lock is a lock of the connection on the key of the codes' making (`pg_try_advisory_lock`, so a try and a making of the account's codes exclude each other), the wait check commits at once and the hashing runs outside any transaction, so the sign-in wait locks of the username and the source are never held during the hashing; a code counts only if its set was made no earlier than the sign-in code the challenge was made for (codes from before a sign-in code reset never come back, before L4 invalidates them); a `recovery_code` proof counts only while its code's set is live (replacing the codes ends the session); a wrong recovery code is a wrong try of kind `recovery_code` (Q-2026-10-24-182 point 3 changed).

## DL-085 — V1-056 slice 11g-1: the automatic late-payment charge (DL-076 answers 1 to 3)

- **Built (migration `20270210_198`):** at 00:00 Property time on the first day after an Invoice's Due Date the billing worker's pass adds one late-payment charge: 10 percent (the Settings rate of DL-075 when it is built; `app.late_payment_rate_basis_points` returns 10 percent until then) of the amount unpaid at that moment, rounded half-up to the cent. The pass runs as the Property's `billing.generate` service principal after the billing runs, under the worker lock; each Invoice is written in its own READ COMMITTED transaction; the day is marked done in `app.late_payment_charge_runs` only when every candidate was looked at with no failure. The service principal is recorded in new columns (`finalized_by_service`, `created_by_service`); the person columns stay and exactly one of the two is set, so the migration takes no lock on `app.user_accounts` (moving the old foreign keys deadlocked the V1-042 upgrade test). The rate check takes a whole percent from 0 to 10. The pass refuses an instant more than one hour old.
- **Owner answer (card, 2026-10-25 01:43, "No charge"):** an Invoice already overdue on the day the pass first runs gets no charge; the pass covers charge days from its first day on. If the very first pass fails before it finishes its day, the next pass becomes the first day (accepted: no charge is ever added for a day before a finished pass could see it).
- **Readings recorded by Claude:** an Invoice issued after its charge moment gets no charge (the Customer had no time to pay before it); a missed day is caught up by the next pass with the amount unpaid at that day's 00:00; an Invoice of a Lease whose Final Settlement is closed gets no charge (BR-SETTLE-012); a charge that rounds to zero writes nothing; the pass starts 10 seconds after 00:00 and the amount is the one unpaid at 00:00. The database refuses a charge for a day before the pass's first day, so the owner's answer holds even for a direct call. The manual decision route and its database functions stay until 11g-3; until then a person may still record a WAIVE decision before the pass reaches an Invoice.
- **Reading recorded by Claude (first day):** an Invoice whose charge moment is 00:00 on the pass's first day was not yet overdue before that day, so it is charged even when the first pass starts later that day; only Invoices overdue before the first day get no charge.
- **Accepted in review round 2:** one Invoice that fails on every pass keeps its day open, so later passes re-read the days since then (new days are still charged; the worker reports failure); slice 12 records a failed Invoice so the day can close. Details in ops/reviews/V1-056-slice-11g-1.md.
- **Test name kept:** `test_review_due_date_boundary_is_property_local_and_never_posts_automatically` still holds for the review it checks (the review posts nothing); its trace entry is in a frozen part of the manifest, so it is not renamed.
- **Migration head:** `20270210_198` (the V1-058 screen rebuild branch also uses the ids 196 to 198; whichever merges second renames its ids and re-chains).
- **Decision date:** 2026-10-25.

## DL-086 — V1-056 slice 11g-2: reduce or waive a Late-payment Charge (DL-076 answer 4)

- **Built (migration `20270211_199`):** `POST /api/v1/late-payment-charges/{charge_id}/reductions` sets a lower amount (0 waives the charge) with one of the three fixed reasons ("Staff recorded the payment on the wrong Invoice", "Paid on time but recorded late", "Other staff mistake") and a "What happened" text of 1 to 500 characters. History keeps every change: the correction row (actor, time, previous and resulting amount) and the new append-only `app.late_payment_charge_reductions` row (reason, text, released value).
- **Paid part (DL-076 reading (d)):** paid value above the new amount is released at once, through the release records of migration `20261117_113`: the paying sources are reversed whole, newest first; the unreleased rest of the last one is posted again to the charge; released Payment value becomes Customer Credit of the charge's Customer (BR-CREDIT-014, also when a third party paid) and released Credit value returns to its own Credit. The released Credit is not used for other debt by this command; staff use it as any Credit (DL-077 answer 5).
- **Readings decided by Claude under the owner's 2026-10-23 22:30 rule (who acts and how, not how much):** the command is one step for a holder of `late_payment.charge_correction` (in the default Owner and Manager bundles only; DL-076 reading (c)), with no draft and no second approver, because DL-076 gives the change to the Owner or a Manager directly; the Customer's complaint is described in "What happened", not checked by the app; a charge a Deposit application paid is refused (only a Final Settlement applies Deposits); a charge paid again from another Payment or Credit while the command waited is refused and the staff member tries again; after the Final Settlement is closed this command is refused and the post-settlement corrections of BR-SETTLE-013 apply.
- **Not changed:** the corrections route and its reduction reversal stay until slice 11g-3 removes the free correction routes. One added refusal: the corrections route does not reverse a reduction made by this route (409), because its paid value was already released as Credit.
- **Checks:** "What happened" has no white space at either end and no C0 or C1 control character other than tab, line feed and carriage return, checked by the API, the service and the database (the database judges white space by its locale, never wider than the API, so the API is the strict side). The command locks the Payments of the paying sources through their serializer in id order, then the Credits, then the charge and its Invoice, as the Final Settlement corrections do; on this route a detected deadlock or serialization failure answers 409 so the client reads the charge and tries again.
- **Migration head:** `20270211_199` (the V1-058 screen rebuild branch also uses ids from 196; whichever merges second renames its ids and re-chains).
- **Decision date:** 2026-10-25.

## DL-087 — V1-056 slice 11g-3: no manual late-payment decision and no free charge correction (DL-076 answers 1 and 4)

- **Type:** `IMPLEMENTATION RECORD`
- **Built (migration `20270212_200`):** from the Property's first finished automatic pass on (a row in `app.late_payment_charge_runs`), `app.finalize_late_payment_decision` refuses a person's decision and `app.correct_late_payment_charge` refuses a REDUCTION, a CHARGE_REVERSAL and a REDUCTION_REVERSAL (P4603, 409 `CONFLICT`). The refusals come after the replay check, so an exact repeat of an earlier request still gets its stored answer. A charge then changes only by the reductions route of DL-086 (one of three fixed reasons, only down). Decisions and corrections recorded before stay as history. Once a finished pass has covered the Invoice's charge day (the day after its Due Date), the late-payment review adds the blocker `AUTOMATIC_CHARGE_ONLY` (not eligible), so the Final Settlement preview no longer raises `LATE_PAYMENT_DECISION_MISSING` for an overdue Invoice the pass did not charge (an Invoice overdue before the first pass, owner answer of 2026-10-25), which no one could clear any more; before a pass has covered that day the preview still waits for an unpaid or partly paid Invoice, so such a Final Settlement cannot close before the pass writes its charge (review round 2). Known gap from slice 11g-1, on the slice 12 list: an Invoice paid in full after its charge moment but before that day's pass is no longer read by the preview, so a Final Settlement can close first and the pass then writes no charge; the window is normally minutes after 00:00, longer only while a failing Invoice keeps a day open. From the first pass the charge read adds `manual_corrections_open: false`; the key also appears in audit states and stored replies written after the first pass (charges written by the first pass itself lack it, because its run row is written after them), so its absence in an older record does not mean the free corrections were open.
- **Readings decided by Claude under the owner's 2026-10-23 22:30 rule (how, not who or how much):** the two POST routes stay and answer 409 instead of being removed, because their stored answers must still replay and their traceability-frozen tests stay in force; the refusal is in the database, so no client can get around it. The refusal starts at the first finished pass, not at the deploy, so tests and history before it keep working; between the deploy and the first 00:00 pass a person could still record a decision. The old Invoices screen hides the decision form once the review is not eligible (between the first pass and the run that covers an Invoice's charge day the form still shows and saving answers 409) and the free correction form (`manual_corrections_open: false`), so it never saves a request that can only be refused; the screen rebuild (V1-058) shows the reductions form instead. The gate is per Property: a Property whose first pass never finishes (no billing service principal, or a day left open by an Invoice that fails on every pass) keeps the manual commands open; the slice 12 list has the failing-Invoice case. A pass that stops after its first run (the billing service principal turned off, or one Invoice failing on every pass) leaves every later charge day uncovered: a Final Settlement with an Invoice overdue on such a day waits, and no one can clear it by a manual decision. This fails safe (no Settlement closes before its charge); restarting the pass clears it. On the slice 12 list. After the first pass a malformed request to either old route also answers 409 (the refusal comes before the input checks).
- **Not changed:** the Final Settlement late-charge commands (they do not use these functions), the reads, the decision check of DL-085.
- **Migration head:** `20270212_200` (the V1-058 branch also uses ids from 196; whichever merges second re-chains).
- **Decision date:** 2026-10-25.

## DL-088 — V1-056 slice 11g-4: the late-payment charge right after its own Invoice in the payment proposal (DL-076 answer 5)

- **Type:** `IMPLEMENTATION RECORD`
- **Built (migration `20270213_201`):** the payment proposal of a payer's own Payment that names nothing (`NORMAL_CUSTOMER`, no identified Invoice or charge) lists each open late-payment charge of the payer right after its own Invoice, before newer Invoices: order Due Date, issue time, Invoice number, Invoice id, then the Invoice before its charge. The charge of an Invoice already paid keeps its Due Date place. A charge counts against the same bounds as an Invoice. Posting the proposal unchanged writes the charge part as a direct charge allocation (the table keeps proposal batches for Invoice targets); its detail trace names the batch. A reduced charge is proposed at what is still unpaid; a waived or fully paid charge is left out.
- **Not changed (DL-029 stays):** a Payment that names an Invoice or a charge, and a third-party Payment, are proposed exactly as before, with no charge targets. Staff still confirm the proposal (Receive payment); the Customer naming what to pay still changes the order (BR-PAY-024).
- **Readings decided by Claude under the owner's 2026-10-23 22:30 rule (how, not who or how much):** a charge target carries its source Invoice's Due Date, issue time and number so the screen can show where it sits; the old allocation screen shows a charge target as "Late-payment charge of" its Invoice; a charge whose source Invoice is VOID is never proposed (voiding an Invoice with a standing charge is already refused). Two posts at once of batches with both charges and Invoices can end in a detected deadlock (no money moves; the service answers unavailable and the client replays the same command with the same key), as designated batches already could. The audit event of a charge allocation posted from a proposal names no proposal batch; its detail trace does.
- **Migration head:** `20270213_201` (the V1-058 branch also uses ids from 196; whichever merges second re-chains).
- **Decision date:** 2026-10-25.

## DL-091 — V1-056 slice 12b: the scheduled worker bills a late Utility period

- **Type:** `IMPLEMENTATION RECORD`
- **Built (migration `20270216_204`):** DL-071 answer 18. Each scheduled worker pass, after its ordinary runs and within the same bound, bills a `LATE_AFTER_SUCCEEDED_RUN` Utility period by a late Utility run: a successor of the last SUCCEEDED run of the same dates whose snapshot holds only the responsible periods with no Invoice line that no run of those dates ever snapshotted, so a period is billed once and never twice. `app.utility_unbilled_periods`, its route and the catch-up command stay as the safety check; a `NOT_MOVED_IN` period is still billed only by the catch-up command, and a period an earlier run billed or skipped is left to it. Only the scheduled worker starts a late run; one that fails does not stop the late-payment charge pass.
- **Decided by Claude under the owner's 2026-10-23 22:30 rule:** the late Invoice is due on the later of the on-time Due Date (the 5th after the period, BR-UTIL-022) and the day it is issued (the Property's date) plus the Property's configured days (the catch-up command's rule, BR-UTIL-021). A Customer never gets an earlier Due Date than on time, and never an Invoice that is already overdue when issued, also when a late run that stopped on an error is resumed on a later day. The amount is unchanged. The owner may change this.
- **Migration head:** `20270216_204`.
- **Decision date:** 2026-10-25.

## DL-093 — V1-056 slice 12d: a waiting REFUND_RETURN correction also holds the other Lease's Settlement

- **Type:** `IMPLEMENTATION RECORD`
- **Built (migration `20270218_206`):** owner answer (a) to Q-2026-10-20-149 (BR-SETTLE-002, BR-SETTLE-012, BR-SETTLE-013, BR-CREDIT-008, DL-032). `app.final_settlement_preview` lists another Settlement's waiting `REFUND_RETURN` correction draft whose plan overlay gives value back to a Credit held by a person of the Lease, the same way as a `REFUND` draft since sub-slice 10i-4c (`PENDING_DRAFT`, blocking).
